extraction.body: Bitcoin costs around $73,630 on Tuesday evening, roughly €65,960. On the Kraken exchange the price fell as low as $72,585 during the day, its lowest level since August 20. Whether the range between $72,000 and $75,000 holds depends on three things: the 200-day moving average at around $73,150, the outflows from the US funds and whether the US Federal Reserve raises rates in December. What is established: US consumer prices rose more than expected in October, long positions worth around $178 million were forcibly closed within an hour, and the spot ETFs lost money on four of the five trading days of the previous week. Our assessment follows further down: the zone holds only if the fund outflows dry up, and so far there is no sign of that. Where the price could head over the coming months is covered in our bitcoin price prediction. Bitcoin back at its August 20 level: the autumn rally has been wiped out To understand why the area around $73,000 in particular is getting so much attention, you have to go back almost three months. On August 19, bitcoin's low on Kraken was still $64,116. Two days later the daily close was $73,001, a jump of almost 14 percent in 48 hours. Since August 21 the price had not dropped below that mark on a single day, until this Tuesday. Arithmetically, the entire late-summer rise has thus been given back. The 30-day high was $84,840, and the price is now a good 13 percent below it. It is around 42 percent short of the record high of $126,080 from October 6, 2025. Over seven days the price is down 5.3 percent, over 30 days 12.2 percent, both according to CoinGecko data. On Monday bitcoin had still closed at $75,253. In our bitcoin price prediction of November 9, the price stood just below the average of $75,451 at which Strategy bought its holdings. New additions are the inflation report and a daily low that, for the first time since late summer, was below the 200-day moving average. US inflation in October: 0.4 percent instead of 0.3 percent The trigger for Tuesday afternoon's decline was the US consumer price index. Prices rose 0.4 percent month on month in October against an expected 0.3 percent. The core rate excluding energy and food rose 0.3 percent, against a forecast of 0.2 percent. The core rate has thus been running at this pace since August, as CoinMarketCap sums up. Fed governor Christopher Waller had said beforehand that with a core rate like this, a 50 basis point hike in December should also be considered. For bitcoin that is an unfavourable backdrop: higher rates make safe assets such as US Treasuries more attractive and raise the cost of the credit used for leverage on the futures markets. US inflation ran hotter than expected in October, and with it the bets on a rate hike in December. Liquidations: $178 million in long positions in one hour How fragile the market was became clear in the hour after the release. According to CoinGlass data, bets on rising prices worth around $178 million were forcibly closed during that time. A liquidation happens when the collateral posted for a leveraged trade is no longer sufficient: the exchange then sells the position itself, and that sale pushes the price down further. The funding rate on perpetual futures at Deribit has been only just above zero for a week, most recently at around 0.004 percent per eight hours. The futures market is no longer overheated, and part of the leverage has already been squeezed out of the market. Analytics firm Glassnode describes the situation in similar terms: selling from the ETFs and nervous short-term holders are weighing on the price, but part of the leverage has already been flushed out. ETF outflows: $1.28 billion in one week The main reason recoveries are fizzling out quickly at the moment lies with the US spot ETFs. In the previous week the funds lost a net $1.282 billion according to SoSoValue data, the largest weekly outflow since the end of June. Monday added a further $201 million in outflows, $213 million of it from BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust alone, while smaller funds took in a little. Since the start of the year the funds thus show a balance of minus $914 million. As recently as September 22 the annual tally had turned positive, after more than $6 billion of inflows since the start of August, CoinDesk reports. In each of the two previous years the funds had collected more than $20 billion.

Bitcoin’s price fell 1.5% in the last 24 hours, falling to around $72,900 at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the apex cryptocurrency trended in ‘extremely bearish’ territory over the past day. Crypto analyst Michael van de Poppe said in a post on X that Bitcoin has support at its 200-day moving average and another support zone between $70,000 and $71,500. However, he stated that buyers might not be strong enough to push the price through resistance yet. “What I'd like to see: A sweep of the lows towards the lower support zones and then a high-volume candle + reclaim back upwards,” he said, calling it “a strong trigger for trades.” The overall cryptocurrency market slipped around 2% in the last 24 hours, teetering above the $2.5 trillion mark with NVDA stock down over 7% and the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) falling almost 2.5%. Analysts were mulling over whether CEO Jensen Huang would be able to retain his post and, if he were removed, who would take the helm instead, after reports stated that he had a second affair with an executive within the company. Ethereum (ETH), Solana (SOL), and Ripple’s XRP (XRP) also fell alongside Bitcoin. Ethereum’s price fell 1.8% in the last 24 hours, struggling to hold above the $2,000 mark, while Solana’s price also fell 1.8%, in danger of dropping below $80. XRP’s price was down around 2%, trading just above the $1 mark. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Ethereum improved to ‘bearish’ from ‘extremely bearish’ territory over the past day, while sentiment around XRP and Solana remained in the ‘bearish’ zone. Crypto equities fell alongside cryptocurrencies in pre-market on Thursday. Corporate cryptocurrency treasuries Strategy (MSTR), Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR), and Strive (ASST) took the biggest hits. MSTR stock was down nearly 6%, while BMNR stock and ASST shares both dropped around 5.5% each. Strategy faces an additional source of pressure after MSCI said it would remove the company from its global indexes after the November 30 rebalancing. The decision could prompt passive funds tracking those indexes to sell their holdings. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around MSTR trended in ‘bearish’ territory over the past day, while chatter rose to ‘normal’ from ‘low’ levels. Large-cap crypto equities Coinbase (COIN) and USDC stablecoin issuers (CRCL) were also caught in the selloff. COIN stock fell around 4%, while CRCL shares were down around 3.5% in pre-market trade. Bitcoin miners, many of which have turned to renting out power and space to AI data centers, were caught on both sides of the sell-off. extraction.body: Firms tied to the Megaspeed controlling shareholder backed the Chinese AI lab as US scrutiny of her Nvidia chip network grows Thu 12 Nov 2026 · 10:06 EST · 3 min read Companies connected to Alice Huang have invested in DeepSeek , the Chinese AI lab known for its competitive open-source models. They also promised it access to Nvidia chips. The timing is awkward. Huang’s main vehicle, Singapore-based Megaspeed International, is already under US investigation over large-scale Nvidia chip imports estimated in the billions of dollars. Huang is a Chinese businesswoman who spent her earlier career in Shanghai’s finance and investment management sectors. She later moved into cloud infrastructure. In March 2023, she became the controlling shareholder of Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud-computing firm. She also served briefly as its managing director. Megaspeed moved quickly after the change in control. The company became an official Nvidia cloud partner shortly after Huang took over. In early 2025, Huang and her associates pitched data-center projects across Southeast Asia. The selling point was guaranteed access to Nvidia GPUs, the graphics processors that power most large-scale AI training and inference. Huang’s network has reportedly facilitated Nvidia AI chip transactions worth billions of dollars. Those deals reportedly involved models such as the H100 and H200, two of Nvidia’s flagship AI accelerators. The DeepSeek investments arrived around November 12, 2026. Firms associated with Huang put money into the lab, with a promise of Nvidia chips attached. Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy. We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime. The problem is everything surrounding the deal. US authorities are examining Megaspeed’s operations, and the investigation centers on the very chip imports that would make such a promise possible. Nvidia’s board has also been reviewing related matters. The chipmaker now finds one of its official cloud partners at the center of a story about chip flows and Chinese AI development. Discussions about possible intelligence ties to Huang’s operations have also surfaced alongside the investment news. Those questions remain open, and nothing in the available material establishes them as fact. Huang’s current status is unclear. Media attention on her business dealings has intensified as the pieces of this network come into view. A Singapore-registered company with an official Nvidia partnership, controlled by a Chinese businesswoman, moving billions of dollars in high-end GPUs, is precisely the type of arrangement regulators tend to examine closely. Add a stake in a leading Chinese AI lab, and the picture becomes harder to explain away as routine cloud business. That does not mean wrongdoing has been proven. The investigations are ongoing, and the intelligence-related questions are still just questions. For Nvidia, the stakes are reputational and potentially regulatory. Its partner program is supposed to signal trust, and a partner under investigation for multibillion-dollar chip imports tests that signal. The board’s review suggests the company is taking the matter seriously. How that review concludes, and whether Megaspeed keeps its partner status, will be worth watching. The key items to track are the outcome of the US investigations into Megaspeed, the result of Nvidia’s board review and any clarification of Huang’s whereabouts and role. sources.title: Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron - Amazon Web Services (AWS)
passages: Today, Amazon announced that SGLang-Neuron is publicly available and can be accessed through an AWS Deep Learning Container, released by RadixArk in collaboration with Annapurna Labs.
With SGLang-Neuron, you can serve models and generate reinforcement learning (RL) rollouts with SGLang on AWS Trainium using the same SGLang interface you use today.
Trainium is a portfolio of AWS AI chips that delivers strong economics for AI training and inference at scale.
Underneath that interface, SGLang-Neuron runs on native PyTorch.
With its out-of-tree plugin design, Trainium support and SGLang core develop independently and iterate faster.
Try it with your workloads, contribute through the project repository, and share feedback to help shape future model and feature support.
Installing the plugin registers the neuron platform through SGLang’s plugin entry points, and setting SGLANG_PLATFORM=neuron selects it when the server starts.
SGLang core continues to provide the API server, request lifecycle, RadixAttention, and prefix-cache bookkeeping.
The plugin implements the Trainium-specific models, attention, mixture of experts (MoE), and the graph runner.
TorchNeuron registers Trainium as a native PyTorch device.

sources.title: AWS Trainium Enhances AI Model Deployment with SGLang-Neuron Integration
passages: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has announced the public availability of SGLang-Neuron, a new integration designed to streamline the deployment of frontier artificial intelligence models on AWS Trainium chips.
SGLang-Neuron utilizes standard PyTorch operations for model execution.
By unifying the serving workflow with familiar SGLang interfaces and leveraging native PyTorch, the integration aims to accelerate AI development and deployment for a wide range of applications.

The SGLang core continues to manage the API server, request lifecycle, RadixAttention, and prefix-cache bookkeeping, while the plugin is responsible for Trainium-specific implementations of models, attention mechanisms, mixture of experts (MoE), and the graph runner.TorchNeuron integrates Trainium as a native PyTorch device.
Upon installation, the plugin registers the Neuron platform through SGLang's plugin entry points.
When starting the server, setting the environment variable SGLANG_PLATFORM=neuron directs SGLang to utilize this new platform.

This collaboration, involving RadixArk and Annapurna Labs, allows developers to leverage the familiar SGLang interface for serving models and generating reinforcement learning rollouts directly on AWS's specialized AI hardware.The Chenab Times has learned that SGLang-Neuron is accessible via an AWS Deep Learning Container, enabling users to maintain their existing SGLang workflows. This means that launching models and invoking endpoints using generation APIs remains unchanged, with SGLang-Neuron handling the underlying execution on AWS Trainium. The integration operates on native PyTorch, and its out-of-tree plugin architecture facilitates independent development and faster iteration between SGLang core and Trainium support.How SGLang Operates on AWS TrainiumSGLang-Neuron functions as an out-of-tree plugin that bridges SGLang with the AWS Trainium platform. Upon installation, the plugin registers the Neuron platform through SGLang's plugin entry points. When starting the server, setting the environment variable SGLANG_PLATFORM=neuron directs SGLang to utilize this new platform. The SGLang core continues to manage the API server, request lifecycle, RadixAttention, and prefix-cache bookkeeping, while the plugin is responsible for Trainium-specific implementations of models, attention mechanisms, mixture of experts (MoE), and the graph runner.TorchNeuron integrates Trainium as a native PyTorch device. SGLang-Neuron utilizes standard PyTorch operations for model execution. For enhanced performance, it incorporates kernels developed with the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI). These operations and kernels are compiled into executable programs using torch.compile, subsequently prepared and run by the graph runner during model serving.The system also supports Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) disaggregation. In this setup, a prefill server computes the prompt KV cache and transfers it to a decode server via NIXL over Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA). Both servers continue to use SGLang’s scheduling and request lifecycle management, while the plugin oversees the Trainium execution and the KV-cache transfer process.Deploying Models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-NeuronUsers can begin deploying models by utilizing a Trainium3 Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance and the pytorch-inference-sglang-neuronx container. The process involves starting the container, launching the SGLang model server with specific configurations for model path, tensor parallelism, expert parallelism, KV cache data type, context length, and memory fraction, and finally sending requests to the model server via its API endpoint.For instance, to serve the OpenAI gpt-oss-120b model, users would execute commands within the container to start the SGLang server, specifying parameters such as --model-path openai/gpt-oss-120b, --tp-size 8, and --ep-size 8, among others. Once the server is running, requests can be made to the /v1/chat/completions endpoint using standard cURL commands.Further details on setup, supported models, features, and configurations can be found in the SGLang-Neuron getting started guide and repository documentation.ConclusionThe introduction of SGLang-Neuron represents a significant step in making advanced AI model deployment more accessible and efficient on AWS Trainium. By unifying the serving workflow with familiar SGLang interfaces and leveraging native PyTorch, the integration aims to accelerate AI development and deployment for a wide range of applications.

extraction.body: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has announced the public availability of SGLang-Neuron, a new integration designed to streamline the deployment of frontier artificial intelligence models on AWS Trainium chips. This collaboration, involving RadixArk and Annapurna Labs, allows developers to leverage the familiar SGLang interface for serving models and generating reinforcement learning rollouts directly on AWS's specialized AI hardware.The Chenab Times has learned that SGLang-Neuron is accessible via an AWS Deep Learning Container, enabling users to maintain their existing SGLang workflows. This means that launching models and invoking endpoints using generation APIs remains unchanged, with SGLang-Neuron handling the underlying execution on AWS Trainium. The integration operates on native PyTorch, and its out-of-tree plugin architecture facilitates independent development and faster iteration between SGLang core and Trainium support.How SGLang Operates on AWS TrainiumSGLang-Neuron functions as an out-of-tree plugin that bridges SGLang with the AWS Trainium platform. Upon installation, the plugin registers the Neuron platform through SGLang's plugin entry points. When starting the server, setting the environment variable SGLANG_PLATFORM=neuron directs SGLang to utilize this new platform. The SGLang core continues to manage the API server, request lifecycle, RadixAttention, and prefix-cache bookkeeping, while the plugin is responsible for Trainium-specific implementations of models, attention mechanisms, mixture of experts (MoE), and the graph runner.TorchNeuron integrates Trainium as a native PyTorch device. SGLang-Neuron utilizes standard PyTorch operations for model execution. For enhanced performance, it incorporates kernels developed with the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI). These operations and kernels are compiled into executable programs using torch.compile, subsequently prepared and run by the graph runner during model serving.The system also supports Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) disaggregation. In this setup, a prefill server computes the prompt KV cache and transfers it to a decode server via NIXL over Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA). Both servers continue to use SGLang’s scheduling and request lifecycle management, while the plugin oversees the Trainium execution and the KV-cache transfer process.Deploying Models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-NeuronUsers can begin deploying models by utilizing a Trainium3 Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance and the pytorch-inference-sglang-neuronx container. The process involves starting the container, launching the SGLang model server with specific configurations for model path, tensor parallelism, expert parallelism, KV cache data type, context length, and memory fraction, and finally sending requests to the model server via its API endpoint.For instance, to serve the OpenAI gpt-oss-120b model, users would execute commands within the container to start the SGLang server, specifying parameters such as --model-path openai/gpt-oss-120b, --tp-size 8, and --ep-size 8, among others. Once the server is running, requests can be made to the /v1/chat/completions endpoint using standard cURL commands.Further details on setup, supported models, features, and configurations can be found in the SGLang-Neuron getting started guide and repository documentation.ConclusionThe introduction of SGLang-Neuron represents a significant step in making advanced AI model deployment more accessible and efficient on AWS Trainium. By unifying the serving workflow with familiar SGLang interfaces and leveraging native PyTorch, the integration aims to accelerate AI development and deployment for a wide range of applications.

passages: "NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately," the board stated.

Colette Kress has been Nvidia's Executive Vice President and CFO since September 2013; prior to that, she spent 25 years at Cisco and Microsoft , among others.

Nvidia said on Thursday that Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, would be the company’s interim chief executive officer, following the resignation of its longtime leader, Jensen Huang, who admitted to an extramarital affair with a businesswoman U.S. intelligence agencies believe to be a spy for China. “The board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team,” said Harvey C. Jones, the newly named chair of Nvidia’s board of directors in a statement . “We expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.” In a note to Nvidia’s employees, Ms. Kress said she believed “deeply in this company” and called its employees “our greatest strength.” She said Nvidia would have a companywide meeting on Nov. 18 to discuss its future. Ms. Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013, is leading the company as it enters an uncertain next chapter. Under the leadership of Mr. Huang, Nvidia grew from a niche maker of computer chips used for video games to one of the most valuable public companies in the world and the linchpin of the artificial intelligence boom. Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the chips used in the big A.I. projects that are driving the U.S. economy. Ms. Kress, 59, faces a challenging road. She is temporarily taking over a company that has been tightly controlled by her predecessor. Mr. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and had managed all aspects of its business with a flat structure that placed him at the center of its day-to-day operations. AI is a generational, game-changing new technology, and Huang founded Nvidia over three decades ago, so whoever replaces Huang has enormous shoes to fill. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » Nvidia's CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. It's a logical choice. Kress has been CFO of Nvidia for 13 years, is always on conference calls, and knows Nvidia's numbers likely better than anyone. However, another executive is favored to replace Huang in the top job as of this writing. As of 5:53 p.m. ET on Nov. 12, Kalshi assigned a 42% chance that a Nvidia executive named Ian Buck would become Nvidia's next CEO. Kress has the next-highest chance at 13%, and there are others in the running as well. Buck, according to his LinkedIn profile, has been a vice president and general manager of Nvidia for nearly 14 years and has worked at Nvidia for over 22 years. Buck completed his undergraduate studies at Princeton University and then earned a Ph.D. in computer science from Stanford. According to various biographies, Buck was the development lead for Brook, the programming language that enabled developers to leverage the parallel processing capabilities of graphics processing units (GPUs) for general-purpose computing. Buck is also credited with creating CUDA, which stands for Compute Unified Device Architecture. CUDA came out in 2006 and has served as a key moat for Nvidia and its GPUs. CUDA is a parallel computing platform and programming model that helps developers build applications with Nvidia's GPUs. CUDA has become the industry standard for deploying new AI applications, providing Nvidia with a strong moat. Investors can think of CUDA as an operating system that runs only on Nvidia chips. So even though there are competitors that can build chips just as powerful as Nvidia, developers will be less prone to switch because they would have to use a different computing platform that they may not know as well. The Huang scandal and quick departure stunned much of Wall Street, which is why the stock has tanked over the past week. Many analysts and pundits also speculated that there was no succession plan in place prior to the scandal. Buck could make sense for several reasons. Even though Huang is tough to replace, Nvidia still has a great product in high demand. One question, though, is what does innovation look like after Huang. After all, Nvidia frequently releases new chip models. Buck provides investors with reassurance that the product is unlikely to go stale. His hiring would resemble Apple's recent decision to name the longtime Apple executive and former senior vice president of hardware engineering, John Ternus, as its new CEO to replace Tim Cook. "He (Buck) could protect Nvidia's technological edge, but his ability to manage the wider commercial relationships and geopolitical challenges would face scrutiny," Charu Chanana, an investment strategist at the investment bank Saxo, said in a research note, according to the BBC. With Huang gone, there are still many concerns about Nvidia, particularly regarding the company's relationship with China and its sales to foreign companies that may have illegally re-exported the chips to China. Chanana raises an interesting point, as one of Huang's big tasks over the past year-and-a-half has been convincing the Trump administration to allow Nvidia to sell chips in China. Buck may not have experience in this realm, which will likely face even more scrutiny moving forward. While Kalshi offers some insight, the prediction markets platform has certainly been wrong many times before, and we don't know how long it will take Nvidia to name a new CEO -- it could be tomorrow or months from now. There are also other candidates who have a chance of becoming Nvidia's CEO, according to Kalshi, including former Nvidia executive Rene Haas, who is now the CEO of Arm Holdings , and Apple's Chief Hardware Officer Johny Srouji. So even though there are competitors that can build chips just as powerful as Nvidia, developers will be less prone to switch because they would have to use a different computing platform that they may not know as well.

The Huang scandal and quick departure stunned much of Wall Street, which is why the stock has tanked over the past week. Many analysts and pundits also speculated that there was no succession plan in place prior to the scandal.
Buck could make sense for several reasons. Even though Huang is tough to replace, Nvidia still has a great product in high demand. One question, though, is what does innovation look like after Huang.

After all, Nvidia frequently releases new chip models. Buck provides investors with reassurance that the product is unlikely to go stale. His hiring would resemble Apple's recent decision to name the longtime Apple executive and former senior vice president of hardware engineering, John Ternus, as its new CEO to replace Tim Cook.

"He (Buck) could protect Nvidia's technological edge, but his ability to manage the wider commercial relationships and geopolitical challenges would face scrutiny," Charu Chanana, an investment strategist at the investment bank Saxo, said in a research note, according to the BBC.

With Huang gone, there are still many concerns about Nvidia, particularly regarding the company's relationship with China and its sales to foreign companies that may have illegally re-exported the chips to China.

Chanana raises an interesting point, as one of Huang's big tasks over the past year-and-a-half has been convincing the Trump administration to allow Nvidia to sell chips in China. Buck may not have experience in this realm, which will likely face even more scrutiny moving forward.

While Kalshi offers some insight, the prediction markets platform has certainly been wrong many times before, and we don't know how long it will take Nvidia to name a new CEO -- it could be tomorrow or months from now.

There are also other candidates who have a chance of becoming Nvidia's CEO, according to Kalshi, including former Nvidia executive Rene Haas, who is now the CEO of Arm Holdings , and Apple's Chief Hardware Officer Johny Srouji.

It comes after a whirlwind week, which saw the company head and co-founder, Jensen Huang, resign amid multiple allegations of extramarital affairs , including one that involved an alleged Chinese spy and two with company employees. Nvidia immediately named Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, as the interim CEO. It’s possible she could stay on permanently, but the company could also name another candidate for the full-time role. Names that have been floated include Ian Buck, who manages Nvidia’s AI hardware and software products, and Rene Haas, a former Nvidia employee and the current CEO of Arm Holdings, a UK-based chipmaker. Whoever takes over from Huang will have tremendous sway in the burgeoning world of artificial intelligence. The entire AI ecosphere relies on Nvidia, which engineers advanced chips used to train AI models and power companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. Nvidia is also a central driver of the US economy and one of the world’s most valuable companies, with a market cap of around $4tn. Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993, is known as an ambitious and visionary CEO who had a hand in most all aspects of the business. He led in an unusual management style, having about 60 direct reports, giving him more control over the company’s daily functions. His son and daughter also work at Nvidia, with his daughter seen as his possible proxy, but neither appear to have sufficient experience to take the helm. Kress, 59, joined Nvidia in 2013 as the CFO after working in finance roles at Texas Instruments, Microsoft and Cisco. She’s a regular contributor to the company’s quarterly earnings calls, and has overseen Nvidia go from a niche firm geared toward video game chips to a trillion-dollar AI juggernaut. People who know her describe Kress as a calming contrast to Huang’s often confrontational style, Reuters reported. “Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” Harvey C Jones, the newly named chair of Nvidia’s board of directors, said in a statement on Thursday. “The board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team.” But that sentiment may not be shared by Huang. During a meeting this past summer, the CEO said Kress was “a deer in the headlights” and interrupted her presentation, a person familiar with the comments told the Wall Street Journal . Huang insinuated during that August meeting that Kress was not someone who could help him make decisions. However, Kress praised Huang in a memo to employees on Thursday, saying she would continue “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years”. Many investors, analysts and industry sources who spoke to Reuters questioned whether a finance executive could preserve the technological risk-taking that turned Nvidia into an AI chips powerhouse. “Putting [Kress] in the interim role makes sense to keep the markets calm, but I don’t think she is the long-term visionary that Nvidia needs to continue its current trajectory,” said Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights and Strategy. Kress, who said in her memo that Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” , will serve as both the CEO and interim CFO until the board names a permanent successor. The board said it was starting a search for Huang’s permanent replacement and is considering internal and external candidates. Along with Kress, Buck is seen as a possible successor. He has worked at Nvidia since 2004 and in charge of deploying generative AI in partnership with the world’s top AI companies, including Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, OpenAI and more. Haas, the CEO of Arm Holdings, is also well-known at Nvidia, having worked there for seven years as a vice president and general manager before joining Arm in 2013. Lisa Su, the CEO of chipmaker AMD, is also being named as a possible replacement for Huang. Her company is Nvidia’s most direct and fierce competitor; she’s also a distant cousin to Huang. Sunny Cheung, an analyst at the Washington-based Jamestown Foundation, said Kress could face congressional questions about the company’s oversight of chip sales involving Chinese military-linked institutions and south-east Asian intermediaries. In a 2023 interview with an Israeli publication, Kress credited her two young sons with urging her to join Nvidia in 2013 because they knew its chips from their video games. She became a billionaire in 2025 based on the value of her Nvidia equity, according to media reports, and Forbes said her net worth of $1.2 billion in mid-2026 put her in 32nd place on its list of America’s richest self-made women. Kress, who holds an undergraduate degree in finance and an MBA, was also named among the 50 most powerful women in business on rankings compiled by Fortune and Forbes magazines in recent years. Nvidia’s CEO turmoil comes as the company is set to report its third-quarter earnings next Tuesday.

Nvidia immediately named Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, as the interim CEO.

Huang insinuated during that August meeting that Kress was not someone who could help him make decisions.

However, Kress praised Huang in a memo to employees on Thursday, saying she would continue “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years”. He has worked at Nvidia since 2004 and in charge of deploying generative AI in partnership with the world’s top AI companies, including Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, OpenAI and more. Haas, the CEO of Arm Holdings, is also well-known at Nvidia, having worked there for seven years as a vice president and general manager before joining Arm in 2013. Lisa Su, the CEO of chipmaker AMD, is also being named as a possible replacement for Huang. Her company is Nvidia’s most direct and fierce competitor; she’s also a distant cousin to Huang. Sunny Cheung, an analyst at the Washington-based Jamestown Foundation, said Kress could face congressional questions about the company’s oversight of chip sales involving Chinese military-linked institutions and south-east Asian intermediaries. In a 2023 interview with an Israeli publication, Kress credited her two young sons with urging her to join Nvidia in 2013 because they knew its chips from their video games. Kress, who holds an undergraduate degree in finance and an MBA, was also named among the 50 most powerful women in business on rankings compiled by Fortune and Forbes magazines in recent years. Nvidia’s CEO turmoil comes as the company is set to report its third-quarter earnings next Tuesday.

sources.title: Microsoft has an image problem with November's Windows security update - The Register
passages: Printer problems aren't the only issue requiring attention.

After installation of the November 2026 security update, Microsoft warned that "certain Windows activation and licensing operations performed using the Software Licensing Management Tool (SLMGR) might fail."

Printing with Windows has always been something of a choose-your-own-adventure, and November's security update has added another unwelcome plot twist: documents containing certain images might not print.

"Affected devices might encounter error 0x80041008 , Invalid parameter ( SWbemObjectEx ), when running commands to activate Windows, configure Key Management Service (KMS), or manage product keys," Microsoft said.
"The failure has been observed while executing the command ' slmgr.vbs /skms-domain ' and ' slmgr.vbs /ipk '."
After the update, those invisible objects can apparently make the printed document disappear too.
Microsoft said: "The issue was observed when printing Microsoft Word documents using the Windows Graphics Device Interface (GDI), but printing from other applications might also be affected."
According to the notification (WI1549472), most versions of Windows are affected, from the latest Windows 11 26H2 through Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2016.
Windows Server from 2025 to 2016 is also affected.
The printing problem remains under investigation, but Microsoft says a fix for the activation issue is due in the coming days.
Administrators needing an interim workaround must contact Microsoft Support for Business. ®
Users need not have added these objects themselves.
Microsoft says document-generation tools can insert them even when no graphic is visible.
This one is a little more niche, but it could be a headache for affected administrators.

Printing with Windows has always been something of a choose-your-own-adventure, and November's security update has added another unwelcome plot twist: documents containing certain images might not print.

"Affected devices might encounter error 0x80041008 , Invalid parameter ( SWbemObjectEx ), when running commands to activate Windows, configure Key Management Service (KMS), or manage product keys," Microsoft said.
"The failure has been observed while executing the command ' slmgr.vbs /skms-domain ' and ' slmgr.vbs /ipk '."
After the update, those invisible objects can apparently make the printed document disappear too.
Microsoft said: "The issue was observed when printing Microsoft Word documents using the Windows Graphics Device Interface (GDI), but printing from other applications might also be affected."
According to the notification (WI1549472), most versions of Windows are affected, from the latest Windows 11 26H2 through Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2016.
Windows Server from 2025 to 2016 is also affected.
The printing problem remains under investigation, but Microsoft says a fix for the activation issue is due in the coming days.
Administrators needing an interim workaround must contact Microsoft Support for Business. ®

extraction.body: Original Secure Boot certificates will soon expire for most Windows users. There is now more reason than ever for Windows 10 users to enroll in the Microsoft Extended Security Updates program. Microsoft officially ended support for Windows 10 on Oct. 14, 2025, yet nearly 1 billion computers worldwide were still running the outdated operating system at the end of the year. Now there is more urgency for Windows 10 users to upgrade to Windows 11 . On Tuesday, Microsoft announced that the original Secure Boot certificates — which prevent Windows machines from running insecure software — would expire in June 2026. To avoid the risk of expired certificates, people will need to either upgrade from Windows 10 or enroll in the Microsoft Extended Security Updates program. To give its users more time to upgrade their software and hardware to Windows 11 , Microsoft has promised to continue supporting Windows 10 with one more year of security updates . Anyone with Windows 10 can enroll in Extended Security Updates and continue receiving updates through Oct. 13, 2026. Microsoft says the ESU program is “not intended as a long-term solution but rather as a temporary bridge to stay secure while one migrates to a newer, supported platform.” Windows security vulnerabilities are serious business. The ESU program is necessary for any users who can’t or don’t want to upgrade to Windows 11 . The cost to enroll in Microsoft’s ESU program is $30, but Europeans can enroll for free . For the rest of the world, there are two other free enrollment options: You can either use Windows Backup and sync your settings to your OneDrive account or redeem 1,000 Microsoft Rewards points. Make sure you’re running the latest version of Windows 10, version 22H2 . You can check your Windows version in Settings . Then, click Windows Update and select View Update History . You also need to have administrative privileges on your PC. Once you confirm the update, visit Settings and Windows Update . Look for the links in the top right corner of the interface. It should read, “Windows 10 support ends in October 2025” and “Enroll in Extended Security Updates to help keep your device secure.” Below that messaging is a link to enroll, which will pop-up the Extended Security Updates enrollment wizard. You need to decide whether you want to sync your settings with OneDrive, pay $30 or use 1,000 Microsoft Rewards points for the ESU program. You can enroll in the ESU program at any time until Oct. 13, 2026. The ESU program is only a temporary solution designed to give users more time to upgrade, although businesses can purchase up to three additional years of updates. Microsoft offers detailed instructions on how to enable Extended Security Updates for Windows 10, but the option to enroll in the program may not yet be available for all eligible users. It appears that Microsoft is still rolling out the enrollment wizard to all locations and devices. We were unable to get the “Enroll now” link or messaging on our CNET test computer running Windows 10, even though we had installed the necessary update (the August 2025 patch KB5063709 ). We reached out to Microsoft for clarification on the timeline for the ESU program. A spokesperson said, “We’re working to restore the availability of the Windows 10 Extended Security Updates program in a subset of markets.” There are two ways to enroll in the Windows Extended Security Updates program for free. You can sync your Windows settings with a OneDrive account connected to your PC or redeem 1,000 Microsoft Rewards points. Unless you have a surplus of Microsoft Rewards points, you need to save your PC data with Windows Backup to get the free security updates for Windows 10. This feature is normally intended to help you save your files as you transfer them from one PC to another. In the ESU enrollment wizard, you’ll see three choices. To sign up for free, select the first option, Back up your PC settings , and click Next to start syncing your settings with OneDrive using your Microsoft account. Windows 10 users who back up their settings automatically to OneDrive will qualify for free extended Windows updates. There is one possible drawback to syncing with OneDrive to get free security updates: You may not have enough storage space. Microsoft only provides 5GB of free storage. If you have a lot of settings data to back up, you might end up paying more. Windows 10 has had an impressive 10-year run, but the operating system isn’t going to receive any updates at all after Oct. 13, 2026. Still, for many users aren’t ready or able to dive into Windows 11, the free Microsoft ESU program is a welcome stopgap. © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. All rights reserved.

Once you confirm the update, visit Settings and Windows Update . Look for the links in the top right corner of the interface. It should read, “Windows 10 support ends in October 2025” and “Enroll in Extended Security Updates to help keep your device secure.”

It appears that Microsoft is still rolling out the enrollment wizard to all locations and devices. We were unable to get the “Enroll now” link or messaging on our CNET test computer running Windows 10, even though we had installed the necessary update (the August 2025 patch KB5063709 ).

coreStoryFacts.text: "When attempting to install the November 2026 Windows security update (the Originating KBs listed above), some devices might be unable to complete the installation.
This is not the first time Microsoft has had to address Windows update installation issues since the start of the year.
In March, it had to pull a buggy Windows 11 non-security preview update (KB5079391) because of 0x80073712 errors during installation.
They caused Sage to crash on multiple workstations.
We had to uninstall the update from the affected workstations to restore functionality, and are waiting to hear what the actual fix is.
I also ran into another issue with the October Windows updates.
Microsoft started blocking older NTLM-based single sign-on authentication in Windows 11 24H2+, which broke our PEAP/MS-CHAPv2 Wi-Fi authentication.
Updated workstations could no longer connect to our authenticated SSID.

Microsoft also told IT administrators that the installation issues will resolve automatically for all affected customers by Friday morning and that end users do not need to take any action to receive the fix.

extraction.body: Original Secure Boot certificates will soon expire for most Windows users. There is now more reason than ever for Windows 10 users to enroll in the Microsoft Extended Security Updates program. Microsoft officially ended support for Windows 10 on Oct. 14, 2025, yet nearly 1 billion computers worldwide were still running the outdated operating system at the end of the year. Now there is more urgency for Windows 10 users to upgrade to Windows 11 . On Tuesday, Microsoft announced that the original Secure Boot certificates — which prevent Windows machines from running insecure software — would expire in June 2026. To avoid the risk of expired certificates, people will need to either upgrade from Windows 10 or enroll in the Microsoft Extended Security Updates program. To give its users more time to upgrade their software and hardware to Windows 11 , Microsoft has promised to continue supporting Windows 10 with one more year of security updates . Anyone with Windows 10 can enroll in Extended Security Updates and continue receiving updates through Oct. 13, 2026. Microsoft says the ESU program is “not intended as a long-term solution but rather as a temporary bridge to stay secure while one migrates to a newer, supported platform.” Windows security vulnerabilities are serious business. The ESU program is necessary for any users who can’t or don’t want to upgrade to Windows 11 . The cost to enroll in Microsoft’s ESU program is $30, but Europeans can enroll for free . For the rest of the world, there are two other free enrollment options: You can either use Windows Backup and sync your settings to your OneDrive account or redeem 1,000 Microsoft Rewards points. Make sure you’re running the latest version of Windows 10, version 22H2 . You can check your Windows version in Settings . Then, click Windows Update and select View Update History . You also need to have administrative privileges on your PC. Once you confirm the update, visit Settings and Windows Update . Look for the links in the top right corner of the interface. It should read, “Windows 10 support ends in October 2025” and “Enroll in Extended Security Updates to help keep your device secure.” Below that messaging is a link to enroll, which will pop-up the Extended Security Updates enrollment wizard. facts.text: "When attempting to install the November 2026 Windows security update (the Originating KBs listed above), some devices might be unable to complete the installation.
This is not the first time Microsoft has had to address Windows update installation issues since the start of the year.
In March, it had to pull a buggy Windows 11 non-security preview update (KB5079391) because of 0x80073712 errors during installation.
They caused Sage to crash on multiple workstations.
We had to uninstall the update from the affected workstations to restore functionality, and are waiting to hear what the actual fix is.
I also ran into another issue with the October Windows updates.
Microsoft started blocking older NTLM-based single sign-on authentication in Windows 11 24H2+, which broke our PEAP/MS-CHAPv2 Wi-Fi authentication.
Updated workstations could no longer connect to our authenticated SSID.
Microsoft fixes audio issues caused by September security updates

Microsoft also told IT administrators that the installation issues will resolve automatically for all affected customers by Friday morning and that end users do not need to take any action to receive the fix.
Microsoft: Recent Windows updates cause SQL Server performance issues
The company also urged admins still receiving reports of installation issues after 48 hours to contact Microsoft Support.
Microsoft fixes Smart App Control broken by October Windows update
Microsoft says October updates didn’t actually fix VPN issues
See what's getting through with a 14-day read-only scan of Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, with no MX changes.
On prem Sage is crashing for my users and can confirm this issue.
Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,235 flaws, Outlook zero-day
Printer problems aren't the only issue requiring attention.

After installation of the November 2026 security update, Microsoft warned that "certain Windows activation and licensing operations performed using the Software Licensing Management Tool (SLMGR) might fail."

Printing with Windows has always been something of a choose-your-own-adventure, and November's security update has added another unwelcome plot twist: documents containing certain images might not print.

"Affected devices might encounter error 0x80041008 , Invalid parameter ( SWbemObjectEx ), when running commands to activate Windows, configure Key Management Service (KMS), or manage product keys," Microsoft said.
"The failure has been observed while executing the command ' slmgr.vbs /skms-domain ' and ' slmgr.vbs /ipk '."
After the update, those invisible objects can apparently make the printed document disappear too.
Microsoft said: "The issue was observed when printing Microsoft Word documents using the Windows Graphics Device Interface (GDI), but printing from other applications might also be affected."
According to the notification (WI1549472), most versions of Windows are affected, from the latest Windows 11 26H2 through Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2016.
Windows Server from 2025 to 2016 is also affected.
The printing problem remains under investigation, but Microsoft says a fix for the activation issue is due in the coming days.
Administrators needing an interim workaround must contact Microsoft Support for Business. ®
Users need not have added these objects themselves.
Microsoft says document-generation tools can insert them even when no graphic is visible.
This one is a little more niche, but it could be a headache for affected administrators.

passages: This is exactly what Elon Musk is doing with his Terafab project, which he first mentioned in November 2025 .

Jensen Huang even warned that this was going to be a challenge, pointing out that “the engineering, the science, and the artistry of doing what TSMC does for a living is extremely hard.” Nevertheless, Musk poured his resources into the project, with construction on the Terafab facility in full swing and with plans to hit volume chip production by the second half of 2028 .
Musk himself said that the site targets a production capacity of a million wafers a month by 2032.
Tesla has an ambitious AI accelerator roadmap , and SpaceX has even touted making its own GPUs in the future .

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO two weeks after his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy was revealed by intelligence sources and a day after his affair with an Nvidia vice president became publicly known.
But hours before this move, when it was just rumored that the Nvidia board was planning to oust him , Elon Musk had already stated his willingness to hire the former Nvidia chief on X .
A random X user posted, “Elon please hire Jensen,” to which the billionaire replied, “That would be an honor.”
This includes former Boeing CEO Harry Stonecipher in 2005, HP CEO Mark Hurd in 2010, Intel CEO Brian Krzanich in 2018, and former McDonald’s CEO Steve Easterbrook in 2019.

Musk himself is known to have had relationships with subordinates from his various companies, and that he has even fathered four children with Shivon Zilis, a top executive at Neuralink who started working at Tesla in 2017, through IVF.
It’s still not confirmed if Musk’s reply is a serious offer for Jensen Huang.

He had rock star status, and now the artificial intelligence industry is weighing who can fill the shoes of Jensen Huang after his forced exit from US chip king Nvidia left the "central bank of AI" without its longtime leader. Huang's abrupt fall comes at a sensitive time for the sector, just days before the closely watched IPO of AI firm Anthropic and amid mounting concerns about the financial soundness of the industry's colossal investment spree. Before his resignation on Thursday after details emerged about multiple extramarital affairs, including with a suspected Chinese spy, Huang had positioned himself as a major booster for the AI industry across both political and financial lines. He had built close ties to Donald Trump, accompanying him on Air Force One earlier this year when the US president traveled to Beijing for a summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. And while other executives called for slowing down AI development over safety concerns, Huang pushed for plowing forward -- perhaps not surprising from the head of a company that has poured billions into companies, data centers and chip deals from which it stands to profit. Those efforts sparked questions about so-called circular dealmaking, highlighting the potentially fragile nature of Nvidia's financing activities. Among those deals was a more than $100 billion financing guarantee for a new data center in Ohio for ChatGPT-maker OpenAI. Nvidia has also committed to buying $10 billion worth of shares in Anthropic's IPO next week. The chip designer's growth appears solid for now, with TF International Securities analyst Ming-Chi Kuo writing on X that the CEO transition would not affect Nvidia's "product development and competitiveness" until 2028 at the earliest. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO on Thursday. But expect "chaos," warned Gary Marcus, a longtime tech industry critic, who wrote on Substack that "things will clearly never be the same, neither for Nvidia, nor the AI industry as a whole. Congressional investigations will continue. The market may crash." Huang persuaded Trump to allow sales of some of Nvidia's high-end chips to China, despite the rivalry between the two countries and existing export controls. Huang will now be absent when the US president meets Xi next week at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. In a note published Thursday, analyst Dan Ives called the whole saga a "black eye moment" for Huang. However, the situation might "sharpen the sword in the battle and arms race" between the US and China, the note continued. Huang's resignation also presents an opportunity for the industry. "Other US tech leaders are now going to have [to] step in," Ives wrote, pointing to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Google CEO Sundar Pichai and Apple Chairman Tim Cook, among others. Major Silicon Valley figures lamented Huang's departure, crediting him with putting Nvidia at the center of the AI boom. "A sad day for Nvidia, developers, America, and all humanity," Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney wrote on X. Sweeney said Huang had built one of the few companies to reach massive scale while continuing to innovate, while others "fell into the trap" of choosing profits over innovation. Clement Delangue, CEO of AI platform Hugging Face, which is owned by Nvidia, called it "a really sad day," saying: "This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened." Delangue vowed to "keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever." "Infidelity is obviously bad," wrote Shaun Maguire, a partner at venture capital firm Sequoia Capital. "But his contributions to American innovation and AI leadership cannot be overstated." Maguire warned that Huang's exit would leave "a huge void," adding that "the American AI community needs to work double-time in an attempt to fill this void." Elon Musk, the world's richest person, said in a video clip shared on X that it would be "an honor" to hire Huang.

extraction.body: The abrupt resignation of Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, on Thursday morning after revelations that he had extramarital affairs with two women sent shock waves through the A.I. industry and spurred calls on Capitol Hill for investigations into whether U.S. security had been compromised. Mr. Huang, the co-founder and chief executive of the Silicon Valley chip giant, stepped down after Nvidia’s board started an inquiry into allegations that he had extramarital affairs with a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies have concluded was spying for China, as well as with an executive who reported to him. It was the stunning fall of one of the most powerful figures in the A.I. boom. Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the advanced chips that are an essential component of artificial intelligence projects. It also touched the White House, where Mr. Huang long had a firm ally in President Trump. The president defended Mr. Huang all week and praised him again on Thursday for doing a “fantastic job”; Mr. Trump then recommended that Tim Cook, the former Apple chief executive, take the helm at Nvidia. A series of reports by The New York Times showed that Mr. Huang, 63, had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman who had been recruited by China’s main spy agency to gather information on Mr. Huang. The Times also reported that Mr. Trump had been warned about the relationship but took no action. U.S. officials suspect that Megaspeed, the Singaporean company where Ms. Huang was a top executive, has helped to smuggle restricted chips into China. Ms. Huang has not responded to requests for comment; China has rejected the espionage claims and called the smuggling allegations “smears.” Nvidia’s board : The board did not mention Mr. Huang’s conduct in its statement announcing his resignation. Instead, it thanked him for his “immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.” Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer , will serve as interim chief executive while the search for a permanent replacement is carried out, it said. Another affair: Mr. Huang had a second extramarital relationship with an executive who reported to him, according to five people who worked at the company, The Times reported on Wednesday. He is the latest member to join a growing club of chief executives brought down by affairs. A long-term strategy: China’s intelligence services have for decades used romantic entanglements to compromise or extract information from prominent people. Although the use of seduction in espionage is not unique to China, the country’s use of it differs in the amount of time it is willing to invest. Read more › Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee as Mr. Huang’s affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy raises national security concerns. Senator Tim Scott, Republican of South Carolina, on Thursday evening sent letters to Mr. Huang and Mr. Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. Mr. Huang resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive on Thursday. But that has not appeared to slow a bipartisan push for more information on whether he had compromised national security. Senator Chuck Schumer of New York, the Democratic leader, said in a social media post that Congress must “demand answers” from Mr. Huang. Mr. Schumer also called on the Trump administration to “answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.” Mr. Lutnick’s department was required to review companies for national security risks before the Trump administration allowed Nvidia to sell advanced chips to China last year. The top Democrats on two congressional committees also wrote to Mr. Lutnick on Thursday, saying they were investigating the matter. My colleagues and I went on Hard Fork, the New York Times podcast about the future of technology, to discuss Jensen Huang’s resignation and its impact on the global tech industry. Listen to or watch it here . House Republicans said they were in discussions with Jensen Huang to get him to testify before Congress sometime this month. Representatives Brian Mast of Florida, who leads the Foreign Affairs Committee, and John Mooelnar of Michigan, who leads a different House committee focused on China, separately told reporters that they had been working to confirm a date and format for Huang to discuss allegations that he had an affair with a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies have concluded was spying for China. Huang’s testimony is not yet scheduled, and it is not clear whether his testimony would be public. Nvidia shares recovered most of their losses in the market by the close of trading, finishing more than 4 percent lower. The stock had fallen by as much as 14 percent Thursday morning after the resignation of Jensen Huang was announced. But as investors’ fears about the company’s future without Huang eased, the shares rebounded. Senator John Thune, Republican of South Dakota and the majority leader, told reporters at the Capitol on Thursday that he anticipated Congress would conduct oversight into Jensen Huang’s apparent involvement with an alleged Chinese spy, even though Huang has resigned as chief executive of Nvidia. “It would make sense because of the nature of the association,” he said. The Democratic leader, Senator Chuck Schumer of New York, said in a social media post that Congress must “demand answers” from Huang and Nvidia officials about “how they may have put U.S. national security at risk.” He added the Trump administration “must answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.” Over the past week, some of Silicon Valley’s most influential investors had argued that America could not win the A.I. race without Jensen Huang, casting his relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy as a personal lapse that should be forgiven because of his importance to the industry. Some kept making that argument even after The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had a relationship with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, hours before his resignation. “Sadly, greatness doesn’t guarantee goodness,” Sarah Guo, a venture capitalist, wrote on X late Wednesday. On Thursday, she called his resignation “a big loss.” Jensen Huang was just becoming one of America’s biggest philanthropists before his departure as the chief executive of Nvidia. With an estimated net worth of about $145 billion , he and his wife, Lori, had built one of the country’s largest foundations, with about $9 billion in assets. But Mr. Huang said this week that he had been unfaithful to his wife, acknowledging an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence has determined was a Chinese spy. The Times then reported that he had another affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him. Nvidia said on Thursday morning that Mr. Huang was resigning from the company he had led for 33 years. The fate of the foundation, which the couple started in 2007 and oversee together, is not clear. Tim Cook stepped down as chief executive of Apple just over two months ago. It is difficult to imagine him moving to Nvidia, in part because he remains so central at Apple. Cook became Apple’s executive chairman in September and has continued representing the company in Washington and around the world. While Cook might not be as technical as the Nvidia’s ousted founder Jensen Huang, he shares other qualities with Huang that could make him attractive to Nvidia’s board of directors, including experience building a global supply chain and a close relationship with President Trump. When suggesting Cook for the job, Mr. Trump wrote on social media: “A Legend replaces a Legend!” As analysts contemplated in recent days what would happen if Jensen Huang departed Nvidia, several noted that prolonged instability at the company could provide an opening for Google and Amazon. Those companies have invested heavily in developing their own A.I. chips, particularly as cheaper alternatives to Nvidia’s powerful but expensive flagship products. Jensen Huang is by far the largest shareholder in Nvidia, holding a 3.56 percent stake, making him one of the wealthiest people in the world. But he does not have voting power like some of Silicon Valley’s other chief executives, such as Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg. That power — which usually comes from “super voting” shares — can shield chief executives from activist investors, market pressures and the board itself. “If the C.E.O. doesn’t do his job according to 12 or 15 board members, the C.E.O. is let go,” Huang said on a podcast in January. But he added, “there will never be one like me, and the reason for that is because I was raised by the company.” Its loan commitments and financing arrangements would make Nvidia the 10th largest bank in the country, according to an estimate from Ryan Cummings, the chief of staff for the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research. “Nvidia is at the center of this circular financing, and obviously at the center of Nvidia is Jensen Huang,” Mr. Cummings said. “He has been the driving force, pretty inarguably, behind a lot of the A.I. build-out.” Without Mr. Huang in charge, Nvidia’s role could change, Mr. Cummings said. And while it is possible that other companies will step in to fill the gap, that isn’t guaranteed. October 2026: Mr. Huang’s affair with Ms. Huang is reported in The New York Times . November 2026: After Mr. Huang admits the affair, Nvidia’s board says it will conduct an investigation. The New York Times later reports that Mr. Huang also had a relationship with Kimberly Powell , Nvidia’s vice president of health care, who reports to him. On Nov. 12, Nvidia’s board of directors announces that Mr. Huang has resigned . Ms. Kress has benefited from Nvidia’s skyrocketing stock price in recent years. As of March, she owned more than 4.4 million shares in the company, according to its most recent annual report, a stake that was worth about $780.4 million at the time. That makes Ms. Kress one of the largest individual shareholders of Nvidia. Its largest individual shareholder, with a 3.56 percent stake, is Mr. Huang. Ms. Kress’s transition — as well as that of the permanent successor to Mr. Huang — could be complicated by how Mr. Huang managed Nvidia. He led the company with an executive team of more than 60 people who directly reported to him, many of whom are longtime loyalists. That flat structure will be difficult to unwind. On a podcast in January , Mr. Huang described his executive team as a group of “60 people who could be world-class C.E.O.s for many other companies.”

It was the stunning fall of one of the most powerful figures in the A.I. boom. Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the advanced chips that are an essential component of artificial intelligence projects.

It also touched the White House, where Mr. Huang long had a firm ally in President Trump. The president defended Mr. Huang all week and praised him again on Thursday for doing a “fantastic job”; Mr. Trump then recommended that Tim Cook, the former Apple chief executive, take the helm at Nvidia.

A series of reports by The New York Times showed that Mr. Huang, 63, had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman who had been recruited by China’s main spy agency to gather information on Mr. Huang. The Times also reported that Mr. Trump had been warned about the relationship but took no action.

U.S. officials suspect that Megaspeed, the Singaporean company where Ms. Huang was a top executive, has helped to smuggle restricted chips into China. Ms. Huang has not responded to requests for comment; China has rejected the espionage claims and called the smuggling allegations “smears.”

Nvidia’s board : The board did not mention Mr. Huang’s conduct in its statement announcing his resignation. Instead, it thanked him for his “immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.” Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer , will serve as interim chief executive while the search for a permanent replacement is carried out, it said.

Another affair: Mr. Huang had a second extramarital relationship with an executive who reported to him, according to five people who worked at the company, The Times reported on Wednesday. He is the latest member to join a growing club of chief executives brought down by affairs.

A long-term strategy: China’s intelligence services have for decades used romantic entanglements to compromise or extract information from prominent people. Although the use of seduction in espionage is not unique to China, the country’s use of it differs in the amount of time it is willing to invest. Read more ›

Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee as Mr. Huang’s affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy raises national security concerns.
Senator Tim Scott, Republican of South Carolina, on Thursday evening sent letters to Mr. Huang and Mr. Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee.
Mr. Huang resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive on Thursday. But that has not appeared to slow a bipartisan push for more information on whether he had compromised national security.

Senator Chuck Schumer of New York, the Democratic leader, said in a social media post that Congress must “demand answers” from Mr. Huang. Mr. Schumer also called on the Trump administration to “answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.”

Mr. Lutnick’s department was required to review companies for national security risks before the Trump administration allowed Nvidia to sell advanced chips to China last year. The top Democrats on two congressional committees also wrote to Mr. Lutnick on Thursday, saying they were investigating the matter.

My colleagues and I went on Hard Fork, the New York Times podcast about the future of technology, to discuss Jensen Huang’s resignation and its impact on the global tech industry. Listen to or watch it here .

House Republicans said they were in discussions with Jensen Huang to get him to testify before Congress sometime this month. Representatives Brian Mast of Florida, who leads the Foreign Affairs Committee, and John Mooelnar of Michigan, who leads a different House committee focused on China, separately told reporters that they had been working to confirm a date and format for Huang to discuss allegations that he had an affair with a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies have concluded was spying for China.
Huang’s testimony is not yet scheduled, and it is not clear whether his testimony would be public.

Nvidia shares recovered most of their losses in the market by the close of trading, finishing more than 4 percent lower. The stock had fallen by as much as 14 percent Thursday morning after the resignation of Jensen Huang was announced. But as investors’ fears about the company’s future without Huang eased, the shares rebounded.

Senator John Thune, Republican of South Dakota and the majority leader, told reporters at the Capitol on Thursday that he anticipated Congress would conduct oversight into Jensen Huang’s apparent involvement with an alleged Chinese spy, even though Huang has resigned as chief executive of Nvidia. “It would make sense because of the nature of the association,” he said.

The Democratic leader, Senator Chuck Schumer of New York, said in a social media post that Congress must “demand answers” from Huang and Nvidia officials about “how they may have put U.S. national security at risk.” He added the Trump administration “must answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.”

Over the past week, some of Silicon Valley’s most influential investors had argued that America could not win the A.I. race without Jensen Huang, casting his relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy as a personal lapse that should be forgiven because of his importance to the industry. Some kept making that argument even after The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had a relationship with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, hours before his resignation. “Sadly, greatness doesn’t guarantee goodness,” Sarah Guo, a venture capitalist, wrote on X late Wednesday. On Thursday, she called his resignation “a big loss.”

Jensen Huang was just becoming one of America’s biggest philanthropists before his departure as the chief executive of Nvidia. With an estimated net worth of about $145 billion , he and his wife, Lori, had built one of the country’s largest foundations, with about $9 billion in assets.

But Mr. Huang said this week that he had been unfaithful to his wife, acknowledging an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence has determined was a Chinese spy. The Times then reported that he had another affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him. Nvidia said on Thursday morning that Mr. Huang was resigning from the company he had led for 33 years.
The fate of the foundation, which the couple started in 2007 and oversee together, is not clear.

Tim Cook stepped down as chief executive of Apple just over two months ago. It is difficult to imagine him moving to Nvidia, in part because he remains so central at Apple. Cook became Apple’s executive chairman in September and has continued representing the company in Washington and around the world. While Cook might not be as technical as the Nvidia’s ousted founder Jensen Huang, he shares other qualities with Huang that could make him attractive to Nvidia’s board of directors, including experience building a global supply chain and a close relationship with President Trump.
When suggesting Cook for the job, Mr. Trump wrote on social media: “A Legend replaces a Legend!”

As analysts contemplated in recent days what would happen if Jensen Huang departed Nvidia, several noted that prolonged instability at the company could provide an opening for Google and Amazon. Those companies have invested heavily in developing their own A.I. chips, particularly as cheaper alternatives to Nvidia’s powerful but expensive flagship products.

Jensen Huang is by far the largest shareholder in Nvidia, holding a 3.56 percent stake, making him one of the wealthiest people in the world. But he does not have voting power like some of Silicon Valley’s other chief executives, such as Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg. That power — which usually comes from “super voting” shares — can shield chief executives from activist investors, market pressures and the board itself.

“If the C.E.O. doesn’t do his job according to 12 or 15 board members, the C.E.O. is let go,” Huang said on a podcast in January. But he added, “there will never be one like me, and the reason for that is because I was raised by the company.”

Its loan commitments and financing arrangements would make Nvidia the 10th largest bank in the country, according to an estimate from Ryan Cummings, the chief of staff for the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research.

“Nvidia is at the center of this circular financing, and obviously at the center of Nvidia is Jensen Huang,” Mr. Cummings said. “He has been the driving force, pretty inarguably, behind a lot of the A.I. build-out.”
Without Mr. Huang in charge, Nvidia’s role could change, Mr. Cummings said. And while it is possible that other companies will step in to fill the gap, that isn’t guaranteed.

The New York Times later reports that Mr. Huang also had a relationship with Kimberly Powell , Nvidia’s vice president of health care, who reports to him. On Nov. 12, Nvidia’s board of directors announces that Mr. Huang has resigned .

Ms. Kress has benefited from Nvidia’s skyrocketing stock price in recent years. As of March, she owned more than 4.4 million shares in the company, according to its most recent annual report, a stake that was worth about $780.4 million at the time. That makes Ms. Kress one of the largest individual shareholders of Nvidia. Its largest individual shareholder, with a 3.56 percent stake, is Mr. Huang.

Ms. Kress’s transition — as well as that of the permanent successor to Mr. Huang — could be complicated by how Mr. Huang managed Nvidia. He led the company with an executive team of more than 60 people who directly reported to him, many of whom are longtime loyalists. That flat structure will be difficult to unwind. On a podcast in January , Mr. Huang described his executive team as a group of “60 people who could be world-class C.E.O.s for many other companies.”
