sources.title: Five ways Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia could damage the AI industry
passages: Undeterred, Huang has been coming up with ways to continue financing the boom and keep his company’s revenues growing.
Certainly, he’s authorized a mind-boggling number of so-called circular deals, where Nvidia buys stakes in companies to fund their expansion so they can buy chips.
By some accounts, the company had committed to $750 billion in such deals as of July, Bloomberg reported.
In August, Nvidia got even bolder, agreeing to backstop $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio, CNBC reported .
Nvidia has lost its top salesperson and the AI industry has lost its top hype man.
Even if Huang somehow comes back into the public eye to champion AI again, every interview and meeting will be about his sex life, choices, and national security — not his vision for the industry.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair (and reports of another one with a direct report ) that led the board to oust him on Thursday isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire CEO sex scandal.
These affairs show undeniably poor judgment by Huang and, I’d argue, unchecked hubris on many levels.
Such choices are not only a betrayal of his wife of 40 years, they’re also a liability for his company.
Sleeping with any Nvidia partner is bad enough, but he also chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation.

Even if Alice Huang’s company wasn’t suspected of helping Chinese firms evade chip restrictions (and he was somehow unaware of this), it was still exploiting a legal loophole by renting powerful AI infrastructure to Chinese companies.
Huang also convinced a whole new set of financiers to pony up.
He promised them that the data centers’ Nvidia GPUs could be used as collateral because Nvidia was guaranteeing the chips would retain value.

We’ll have to wait and see how Nvidia navigates the scandal Huang heaped onto it, but now that the company is finally in its post “founder mode” era, and hunting for a new CEO, it’s doubtful it has the cache to push the industry the way Huang was.
Will Democrats, who are set to take over key committees when the new Congress convenes in January, also haul him in to testify on the Hill?
No one knows yet, but Huang has flaunted his close relationship with President Trump.
Remember when Trump called him while he was onstage at the All-In Summit in September?
Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom, a deeply unpopular project with American voters.
Several Democratic lawmakers have already vowed to investigate the money behind it.
Nvidia not only offers its own open-weight models, it also offers a lot of other open source tech for agents, AI security, and more.
It has even agreed to acquire the biggest site that hosts them, Hugging Face, for $12.9 billion. (That deal is supposed to close in the first half of next year, pending regulatory approval.)
As the industry mulled over what they should do ( auditors? a FINRA-like board? ), Huang rallied the tech industry again.
Nvidia got over 100 companies to sign on to his Open Agent Safety Platform, a largely open source effort to solve the epidemic of misbehaving AI agents.
Huang sold a vision of Nvidia as “investable infrastructure” with a long resale cycle, like airplanes.
Then he made the rounds with the financial press, as he often did, to pitch his vision.
Now, however, Wall Street is concerned that Nvidia’s stock will crash and take their portfolios, and possibly the economy, with it .
In this case, one of his lovers is suspected by the U.S. government of being a spy for China .

extraction.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair (and reports of another one with a direct report ) that led the board to oust him on Thursday isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire CEO sex scandal. In this case, one of his lovers is suspected by the U.S. government of being a spy for China . She’s also an executive of a Singapore-based neocloud that is suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China. These affairs show undeniably poor judgment by Huang and, I’d argue, unchecked hubris on many levels. Such choices are not only a betrayal of his wife of 40 years, they’re also a liability for his company. Sleeping with any Nvidia partner is bad enough, but he also chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation. Even if Alice Huang’s company wasn’t suspected of helping Chinese firms evade chip restrictions (and he was somehow unaware of this), it was still exploiting a legal loophole by renting powerful AI infrastructure to Chinese companies. It’s those potential national consequences that may land him in a hellscape of ongoing public humiliation. Republican committee chairs are already summoning him to testify in closed-door sessions about the security ramifications. Will Democrats, who are set to take over key committees when the new Congress convenes in January, also haul him in to testify on the Hill? No one knows yet, but Huang has flaunted his close relationship with President Trump. Remember when Trump called him while he was onstage at the All-In Summit in September? Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom, a deeply unpopular project with American voters. Several Democratic lawmakers have already vowed to investigate the money behind it. In other words, he is a billionaire close to Trump. He was — until Thursday — the face of AI and data centers (also a deeply unpopular political topic with voters), and he has publicly admitted to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Even though he’s no longer CEO, that seems too juicy a target for Democrats to ignore. Beyond whatever may be coming, Huang’s influence has been lost right when he was using it to push the tech industry in a number of directions. These areas have now lost their biggest champion. Huang has been the biggest, loudest advocate for open-weight AI models in the tech industry and among government policymakers. Nvidia not only offers its own open-weight models, it also offers a lot of other open source tech for agents, AI security, and more. It has even agreed to acquire the biggest site that hosts them, Hugging Face, for $12.9 billion. (That deal is supposed to close in the first half of next year, pending regulatory approval.) In July, when Anthropic and OpenAI were reportedly urging the Trump administration to ban Chinese open-weight models, Huang organized a letter of support for open-weight models generally (if not Chinese models specifically), signed by hundreds of tech companies. Open-weight models give enterprises choice in the market and reduce costs. Without Huang, the next biggest advocate for them is perhaps Microsoft’s Satya Nadella, but he’s not out there organizing the industry to speak up. Both OpenAI and Anthropic revealed incident after incident this year as their AI agents hacked into others’ networks or performed other misdeeds. Huang loudly proclaimed the AI industry still didn’t need regulation and would deal with safety itself. As the industry mulled over what they should do ( auditors? a FINRA-like board? ), Huang rallied the tech industry again. Nvidia got over 100 companies to sign on to his Open Agent Safety Platform, a largely open source effort to solve the epidemic of misbehaving AI agents. Naturally, this effort hasn’t instantly solved the problem , and now the top spokesperson for self-regulation via technology solutions is out of his position of influence. Huang has also been among the loudest voices insisting that AI is an engineered system that creates products, and so can be controlled like any other engineered system. This viewpoint counters the AI doomers and even the big AI labs themselves, which sometimes position their models as on the verge of consciousness (Anthropic) or as alien minds (OpenAI) . While Huang deals with the fallout of his actions, the loudest voice of this counter-narrative is, for the foreseeable future, silenced. Huang also just convinced a long list of PC makers to buy into his long-time dream of providing CPUs (the main processor chips) for them. In this age, when most Americans have not experienced AI beyond a chatbot, he orchestrated a new line of high-end AI PCs geared for running agents locally. These new PCs are due out this holiday season, and they may sell well for their intended targets: creators, developers, and others already savvy with agents. But now that Huang has become a meme for cheating on his wife with an alleged spy, he’s perhaps not the best choice to help market these devices as a cool alternative to the Mac mini. Huang demolished his reputation right as bond underwriters (lenders) and bond buyers are pretty much over AI build-out-related debt. Of roughly $80 billion in data center bonds issued this year, nearly half were rated high-risk “junk,” Forbes reports. Undeterred, Huang has been coming up with ways to continue financing the boom and keep his company’s revenues growing. Certainly, he’s authorized a mind-boggling number of so-called circular deals, where Nvidia buys stakes in companies to fund their expansion so they can buy chips. By some accounts, the company had committed to $750 billion in such deals as of July, Bloomberg reported. In August, Nvidia got even bolder, agreeing to backstop $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio, CNBC reported . Huang also convinced a whole new set of financiers to pony up. In August, he announced that deep-pocketed PE firms Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR had committed up to $500 billion for data center build outs . He promised them that the data centers’ Nvidia GPUs could be used as collateral because Nvidia was guaranteeing the chips would retain value. Huang sold a vision of Nvidia as “investable infrastructure” with a long resale cycle, like airplanes. Then he made the rounds with the financial press, as he often did, to pitch his vision. Now, however, Wall Street is concerned that Nvidia’s stock will crash and take their portfolios, and possibly the economy, with it . Nvidia has lost its top salesperson and the AI industry has lost its top hype man. Even if Huang somehow comes back into the public eye to champion AI again, every interview and meeting will be about his sex life, choices, and national security — not his vision for the industry. By some accounts, the company had committed to $750 billion in such deals as of July, Bloomberg reported.
In August, Nvidia got even bolder, agreeing to backstop $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio, CNBC reported .
Nvidia has lost its top salesperson and the AI industry has lost its top hype man.
Even if Huang somehow comes back into the public eye to champion AI again, every interview and meeting will be about his sex life, choices, and national security — not his vision for the industry.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair (and reports of another one with a direct report ) that led the board to oust him on Thursday isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire CEO sex scandal.
These affairs show undeniably poor judgment by Huang and, I’d argue, unchecked hubris on many levels.
Such choices are not only a betrayal of his wife of 40 years, they’re also a liability for his company.
Sleeping with any Nvidia partner is bad enough, but he also chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation.

Even if Alice Huang’s company wasn’t suspected of helping Chinese firms evade chip restrictions (and he was somehow unaware of this), it was still exploiting a legal loophole by renting powerful AI infrastructure to Chinese companies.
Huang also convinced a whole new set of financiers to pony up.
He promised them that the data centers’ Nvidia GPUs could be used as collateral because Nvidia was guaranteeing the chips would retain value.

We’ll have to wait and see how Nvidia navigates the scandal Huang heaped onto it, but now that the company is finally in its post “founder mode” era, and hunting for a new CEO, it’s doubtful it has the cache to push the industry the way Huang was.
Will Democrats, who are set to take over key committees when the new Congress convenes in January, also haul him in to testify on the Hill?
No one knows yet, but Huang has flaunted his close relationship with President Trump.
Remember when Trump called him while he was onstage at the All-In Summit in September?
Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom, a deeply unpopular project with American voters.
Several Democratic lawmakers have already vowed to investigate the money behind it.
Nvidia not only offers its own open-weight models, it also offers a lot of other open source tech for agents, AI security, and more.
It has even agreed to acquire the biggest site that hosts them, Hugging Face, for $12.9 billion. (That deal is supposed to close in the first half of next year, pending regulatory approval.)
As the industry mulled over what they should do ( auditors? a FINRA-like board? ), Huang rallied the tech industry again.
Nvidia got over 100 companies to sign on to his Open Agent Safety Platform, a largely open source effort to solve the epidemic of misbehaving AI agents.
Huang sold a vision of Nvidia as “investable infrastructure” with a long resale cycle, like airplanes.
Then he made the rounds with the financial press, as he often did, to pitch his vision.
Now, however, Wall Street is concerned that Nvidia’s stock will crash and take their portfolios, and possibly the economy, with it .
In this case, one of his lovers is suspected by the U.S. government of being a spy for China .

coreStoryFacts.text: This is exactly what Elon Musk is doing with his Terafab project, which he first mentioned in November 2025 .

Jensen Huang even warned that this was going to be a challenge, pointing out that “the engineering, the science, and the artistry of doing what TSMC does for a living is extremely hard.” Nevertheless, Musk poured his resources into the project, with construction on the Terafab facility in full swing and with plans to hit volume chip production by the second half of 2028 .
Musk himself said that the site targets a production capacity of a million wafers a month by 2032.
Tesla has an ambitious AI accelerator roadmap , and SpaceX has even touted making its own GPUs in the future .

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO two weeks after his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy was revealed by intelligence sources and a day after his affair with an Nvidia vice president became publicly known.
But hours before this move, when it was just rumored that the Nvidia board was planning to oust him , Elon Musk had already stated his willingness to hire the former Nvidia chief on X .
A random X user posted, “Elon please hire Jensen,” to which the billionaire replied, “That would be an honor.”
This includes former Boeing CEO Harry Stonecipher in 2005, HP CEO Mark Hurd in 2010, Intel CEO Brian Krzanich in 2018, and former McDonald’s CEO Steve Easterbrook in 2019.

Musk himself is known to have had relationships with subordinates from his various companies, and that he has even fathered four children with Shivon Zilis, a top executive at Neuralink who started working at Tesla in 2017, through IVF.
It’s still not confirmed if Musk’s reply is a serious offer for Jensen Huang.

The chip designer's growth appears solid for now, with TF International Securities analyst Ming-Chi Kuo writing on X that the CEO transition would not affect Nvidia's "product development and competitiveness" until 2028 at the earliest.
But expect "chaos," warned Gary Marcus, a longtime tech industry critic, who wrote on Substack that "things will clearly never be the same, neither for Nvidia, nor the AI industry as a whole.
Nvidia has also committed to buying $10 billion worth of shares in Anthropic's IPO next week.
Huang persuaded Trump to allow sales of some of Nvidia's high-end chips to China, despite the rivalry between the two countries and existing export controls.
Major Silicon Valley figures lamented Huang's departure, crediting him with putting Nvidia at the center of the AI boom.
Clement Delangue, CEO of AI platform Hugging Face, which is owned by Nvidia, called it "a really sad day," saying: "This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened."
Huang admits the affair, Nvidia’s board says it will conduct an investigation.
Huang also had a relationship with Kimberly Powell , Nvidia’s vice president of health care, who reports to him.

Over the past week, some of Silicon Valley’s most influential investors had argued that America could not win the A.I. race without Jensen Huang, casting his relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy as a personal lapse that should be forgiven because of his importance to the industry.
“Sadly, greatness doesn’t guarantee goodness,” Sarah Guo, a venture capitalist, wrote on X late Wednesday.

Clement Delangue, CEO of AI platform Hugging Face, which is owned by Nvidia, called it "a really sad day," saying: "This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened."
Huang admits the affair, Nvidia’s board says it will conduct an investigation.
Huang also had a relationship with Kimberly Powell , Nvidia’s vice president of health care, who reports to him.

Over the past week, some of Silicon Valley’s most influential investors had argued that America could not win the A.I. race without Jensen Huang, casting his relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy as a personal lapse that should be forgiven because of his importance to the industry.
“Sadly, greatness doesn’t guarantee goodness,” Sarah Guo, a venture capitalist, wrote on X late Wednesday.
On Thursday, she called his resignation “a big loss.”
October 2026: Mr. Huang’s affair with Ms. Huang is reported in The New York Times .
Trump had been warned about the relationship but took no action.
Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee as Mr.
Huang was resigning from the company he had led for 33 years.
The stock had fallen by as much as 14 percent Thursday morning after the resignation of Jensen Huang was announced.

The Democratic leader, Senator Chuck Schumer of New York, said in a social media post that Congress must “demand answers” from Huang and Nvidia officials about “how they may have put U.S. national security at risk.” He added the Trump administration “must answer for what it did once it learned about Mr.
“Nvidia is at the center of this circular financing, and obviously at the center of Nvidia is Jensen Huang,” Mr.
Huang in charge, Nvidia’s role could change, Mr.
Undeterred, Huang has been coming up with ways to continue financing the boom and keep his company’s revenues growing.
Certainly, he’s authorized a mind-boggling number of so-called circular deals, where Nvidia buys stakes in companies to fund their expansion so they can buy chips.
By some accounts, the company had committed to $750 billion in such deals as of July, Bloomberg reported.
In August, Nvidia got even bolder, agreeing to backstop $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio, CNBC reported .
Nvidia has lost its top salesperson and the AI industry has lost its top hype man.
Even if Huang somehow comes back into the public eye to champion AI again, every interview and meeting will be about his sex life, choices, and national security — not his vision for the industry.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair (and reports of another one with a direct report ) that led the board to oust him on Thursday isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire CEO sex scandal.
These affairs show undeniably poor judgment by Huang and, I’d argue, unchecked hubris on many levels.
Such choices are not only a betrayal of his wife of 40 years, they’re also a liability for his company.
Sleeping with any Nvidia partner is bad enough, but he also chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation.

Even if Alice Huang’s company wasn’t suspected of helping Chinese firms evade chip restrictions (and he was somehow unaware of this), it was still exploiting a legal loophole by renting powerful AI infrastructure to Chinese companies.
Huang also convinced a whole new set of financiers to pony up.
He promised them that the data centers’ Nvidia GPUs could be used as collateral because Nvidia was guaranteeing the chips would retain value.

We’ll have to wait and see how Nvidia navigates the scandal Huang heaped onto it, but now that the company is finally in its post “founder mode” era, and hunting for a new CEO, it’s doubtful it has the cache to push the industry the way Huang was.
Will Democrats, who are set to take over key committees when the new Congress convenes in January, also haul him in to testify on the Hill?
No one knows yet, but Huang has flaunted his close relationship with President Trump.
Remember when Trump called him while he was onstage at the All-In Summit in September?
Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom, a deeply unpopular project with American voters.
Several Democratic lawmakers have already vowed to investigate the money behind it.
Nvidia not only offers its own open-weight models, it also offers a lot of other open source tech for agents, AI security, and more.
It has even agreed to acquire the biggest site that hosts them, Hugging Face, for $12.9 billion. (That deal is supposed to close in the first half of next year, pending regulatory approval.)
As the industry mulled over what they should do ( auditors? a FINRA-like board? ), Huang rallied the tech industry again.
Nvidia got over 100 companies to sign on to his Open Agent Safety Platform, a largely open source effort to solve the epidemic of misbehaving AI agents.
Huang sold a vision of Nvidia as “investable infrastructure” with a long resale cycle, like airplanes.
Then he made the rounds with the financial press, as he often did, to pitch his vision.
Now, however, Wall Street is concerned that Nvidia’s stock will crash and take their portfolios, and possibly the economy, with it .
In this case, one of his lovers is suspected by the U.S. government of being a spy for China .

He had rock star status, and now the artificial intelligence industry is weighing who can fill the shoes of Jensen Huang after his forced exit from US chip king Nvidia left the "central bank of AI" without its longtime leader. Huang's abrupt fall comes at a sensitive time for the sector, just days before the closely watched IPO of AI firm Anthropic and amid mounting concerns about the financial soundness of the industry's colossal investment spree. Before his resignation on Thursday after details emerged about multiple extramarital affairs, including with a suspected Chinese spy, Huang had positioned himself as a major booster for the AI industry across both political and financial lines. He had built close ties to Donald Trump, accompanying him on Air Force One earlier this year when the US president traveled to Beijing for a summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. And while other executives called for slowing down AI development over safety concerns, Huang pushed for plowing forward -- perhaps not surprising from the head of a company that has poured billions into companies, data centers and chip deals from which it stands to profit. Those efforts sparked questions about so-called circular dealmaking, highlighting the potentially fragile nature of Nvidia's financing activities. Among those deals was a more than $100 billion financing guarantee for a new data center in Ohio for ChatGPT-maker OpenAI. Nvidia has also committed to buying $10 billion worth of shares in Anthropic's IPO next week. The chip designer's growth appears solid for now, with TF International Securities analyst Ming-Chi Kuo writing on X that the CEO transition would not affect Nvidia's "product development and competitiveness" until 2028 at the earliest. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO on Thursday. But expect "chaos," warned Gary Marcus, a longtime tech industry critic, who wrote on Substack that "things will clearly never be the same, neither for Nvidia, nor the AI industry as a whole. Congressional investigations will continue. The market may crash." Huang persuaded Trump to allow sales of some of Nvidia's high-end chips to China, despite the rivalry between the two countries and existing export controls. Huang will now be absent when the US president meets Xi next week at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. In a note published Thursday, analyst Dan Ives called the whole saga a "black eye moment" for Huang. However, the situation might "sharpen the sword in the battle and arms race" between the US and China, the note continued. Huang's resignation also presents an opportunity for the industry. "Other US tech leaders are now going to have [to] step in," Ives wrote, pointing to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Google CEO Sundar Pichai and Apple Chairman Tim Cook, among others. Major Silicon Valley figures lamented Huang's departure, crediting him with putting Nvidia at the center of the AI boom. "A sad day for Nvidia, developers, America, and all humanity," Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney wrote on X. Sweeney said Huang had built one of the few companies to reach massive scale while continuing to innovate, while others "fell into the trap" of choosing profits over innovation. Nvidia has also committed to buying $10 billion worth of shares in Anthropic's IPO next week.

extraction.body: The abrupt resignation of Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, on Thursday morning after revelations that he had extramarital affairs with two women sent shock waves through the A.I. industry and spurred calls on Capitol Hill for investigations into whether U.S. security had been compromised. Mr. Huang, the co-founder and chief executive of the Silicon Valley chip giant, stepped down after Nvidia’s board started an inquiry into allegations that he had extramarital affairs with a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies have concluded was spying for China, as well as with an executive who reported to him. It was the stunning fall of one of the most powerful figures in the A.I. boom. Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the advanced chips that are an essential component of artificial intelligence projects. It also touched the White House, where Mr. Huang long had a firm ally in President Trump. The president defended Mr. Huang all week and praised him again on Thursday for doing a “fantastic job”; Mr. Trump then recommended that Tim Cook, the former Apple chief executive, take the helm at Nvidia. A series of reports by The New York Times showed that Mr. Huang, 63, had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman who had been recruited by China’s main spy agency to gather information on Mr. Huang. The Times also reported that Mr. Trump had been warned about the relationship but took no action. U.S. officials suspect that Megaspeed, the Singaporean company where Ms. Huang was a top executive, has helped to smuggle restricted chips into China. Ms. Huang has not responded to requests for comment; China has rejected the espionage claims and called the smuggling allegations “smears.” Nvidia’s board : The board did not mention Mr. Huang’s conduct in its statement announcing his resignation. Instead, it thanked him for his “immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.” Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer , will serve as interim chief executive while the search for a permanent replacement is carried out, it said. Another affair: Mr. Huang had a second extramarital relationship with an executive who reported to him, according to five people who worked at the company, The Times reported on Wednesday. He is the latest member to join a growing club of chief executives brought down by affairs. A long-term strategy: China’s intelligence services have for decades used romantic entanglements to compromise or extract information from prominent people. Although the use of seduction in espionage is not unique to China, the country’s use of it differs in the amount of time it is willing to invest. Senator Tim Scott, Republican of South Carolina, on Thursday evening sent letters to Mr. Huang and Mr. Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. Mr. Huang resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive on Thursday. But that has not appeared to slow a bipartisan push for more information on whether he had compromised national security. Senator Chuck Schumer of New York, the Democratic leader, said in a social media post that Congress must “demand answers” from Mr. Huang. Mr. Schumer also called on the Trump administration to “answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.” Mr. Lutnick’s department was required to review companies for national security risks before the Trump administration allowed Nvidia to sell advanced chips to China last year. sources.title: Five ways Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia could damage the AI industry
passages: Undeterred, Huang has been coming up with ways to continue financing the boom and keep his company’s revenues growing.
Certainly, he’s authorized a mind-boggling number of so-called circular deals, where Nvidia buys stakes in companies to fund their expansion so they can buy chips.
By some accounts, the company had committed to $750 billion in such deals as of July, Bloomberg reported.
In August, Nvidia got even bolder, agreeing to backstop $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio, CNBC reported .
Nvidia has lost its top salesperson and the AI industry has lost its top hype man.
Even if Huang somehow comes back into the public eye to champion AI again, every interview and meeting will be about his sex life, choices, and national security — not his vision for the industry.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair (and reports of another one with a direct report ) that led the board to oust him on Thursday isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire CEO sex scandal.
These affairs show undeniably poor judgment by Huang and, I’d argue, unchecked hubris on many levels.
Such choices are not only a betrayal of his wife of 40 years, they’re also a liability for his company.
Sleeping with any Nvidia partner is bad enough, but he also chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation.

Even if Alice Huang’s company wasn’t suspected of helping Chinese firms evade chip restrictions (and he was somehow unaware of this), it was still exploiting a legal loophole by renting powerful AI infrastructure to Chinese companies.
Huang also convinced a whole new set of financiers to pony up.

It’s those potential national consequences that may land him in a hellscape of ongoing public humiliation. Republican committee chairs are already summoning him to testify in closed-door sessions about the security ramifications. Will Democrats, who are set to take over key committees when the new Congress convenes in January, also haul him in to testify on the Hill? Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom, a deeply unpopular project with American voters. Several Democratic lawmakers have already vowed to investigate the money behind it. In other words, he is a billionaire close to Trump. He was — until Thursday — the face of AI and data centers (also a deeply unpopular political topic with voters), and he has publicly admitted to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Even though he’s no longer CEO, that seems too juicy a target for Democrats to ignore. The available evidence does not confirm whether Nvidia's policies include explicit provisions for the chief executive, but the conflict-of-interest framework applies broadly to the company's workforce. Powell joined Nvidia in 2008 and advanced to vice president of government health care after earlier roles in AI business development . No reporting establishes a connection between that progression and the alleged relationship. Nvidia shares fell more than 3% in after-hours trading after the Times published its report, according to CNBC, though that decline likely reflects the cumulative weight of multiple ongoing concerns. The more consequential question is not on a stock ticker. Five people inside Nvidia allegedly knew enough about a reported relationship between the CEO and a direct report to speak with a reporter. Whether any internal process addressed that situation before a law firm was retained for a separate investigation is not established by the available reporting. Nvidia's board faces a governance structure that was not built to scrutinize the person who built the company, and that gap is exactly what an independent review should now examine.

extraction.body: A romantic relationship between a CEO and a vice president who reports directly to him could create a serious conflict of interest. When that relationship is allegedly undisclosed and the executive holds authority over the subordinate's career, compensation, and responsibilities, it becomes a governance problem , not a personal one. The New York Times, citing five people who worked at Nvidia and spoke anonymously, reported that Jensen Huang allegedly had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, who reportedly reports to him. Both Huang and Powell are married to other people, according to the Times. Two of the five anonymous sources told the Times that Huang and Powell were captured on video appearing affectionate at a San Jose hotel during Nvidia's GTC developer conference in March. The Times stated it had not viewed the video, and its existence should not be treated as established. The responses from all three parties were notable mostly for what they were not. Nvidia declined to comment to the Times. Powell did not respond to a request for comment. When the Times reached Huang directly, he said "I don't think you should be talking to me directly" and ended the call. Huang did not expressly deny the allegation in that exchange. This allegation is distinct from the separate matter in which Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in a message to Nvidia employees, according to the BBC. That admission concerned a different alleged relationship, with Alice Huang. U.S. officials reportedly assessed Alice Huang to be a Chinese intelligence asset , an assessment China has denied. Nvidia's board retained Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen and Katz to conduct an independent investigation into that matter, according to CNBC. Whether the scope of that investigation covers the Powell allegation is not public. Nvidia's own code of conduct, as characterized in Times reporting, instructs employees to avoid situations that create conflicts of interest, including those involving personal relationships, and states that the company investigates misconduct reports promptly. A reporting relationship between a CEO and a vice president is exactly what those rules exist to prevent. The available evidence does not confirm whether Nvidia's policies include explicit provisions for the chief executive, but the conflict-of-interest framework applies broadly to the company's workforce. The allegation and the footage described by anonymous sources both remain without independent confirmation. Whether the alleged relationship affected Powell's career trajectory, pay, or responsibilities at Nvidia has not been publicly confirmed. Powell joined Nvidia in 2008 and advanced to vice president of government health care after earlier roles in AI business development . No reporting establishes a connection between that progression and the alleged relationship. Nvidia shares fell more than 3% in after-hours trading after the Times published its report, according to CNBC, though that decline likely reflects the cumulative weight of multiple ongoing concerns. The more consequential question is not on a stock ticker. Five people inside Nvidia allegedly knew enough about a reported relationship between the CEO and a direct report to speak with a reporter. Whether any internal process addressed that situation before a law firm was retained for a separate investigation is not established by the available reporting. Nvidia's board faces a governance structure that was not built to scrutinize the person who built the company, and that gap is exactly what an independent review should now examine.

passages: US House Speaker Mike Johnson has said ⁠there is a ​growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang .
Lawmakers from both parties have called for tougher restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI chips, threatening access to chips that underpin China’s surging AI development.

Donald Trump, who had defended Huang at first as the scandal threatened to overwhelm Nvidia co-founder, quickly moved on to potential successors on Thursday, posting on social media that he should be replaced by Tim Cook, Apple’s former chief executive and current executive chair.
Rene Haas, the chief executive of Arm Holdings, a UK-based chipmaker, has also been mooted, along with Lisa Su, the chief executive of the chipmaker AMD.
On Thursday came reports that the ousted former CEO had an intimate relationship with a second employee.

The revelation, reported by Reuters, follows allegations of two other extramarital ⁠affairs that led to Jensen Huang’s dramatic resignation – one with Alice Huang, ​an alleged Chinese spy, and another with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice-president of health care.

extraction.body: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said on Thursday, according to reports from Bloomberg and NBC News . Huang, who stepped down as CEO following reports of an alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, agreed to testify Wednesday after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him. Huang has agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, which falls later this month. The development comes after House Republicans Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting that he appear before their committees . Moolenaar chairs the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, Mast chairs the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and Crawford chairs the House Intelligence Committee. “Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.” The testimony will take place behind closed doors, though Mast said he expects the briefing to be recorded on video and transcribed.

House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said the testimony is expected before Thanksgiving, according to TechCrunch. Three committees are driving the request: Mast’s House Foreign Affairs Committee, the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party chaired by John Moolenaar, and the House Intelligence Committee chaired by Rick Crawford. The lawmakers sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting his appearance, according to TechCrunch. CNBC reported the session will likely occur under oath , though the final date and format are still being negotiated. Mast said Huang has “very serious questions to answer” and pointed to disagreements over export controls as a specific concern, while also describing Nvidia as an important U.S. company, according to TechCrunch. That framing suggests lawmakers may examine Nvidia’s commercial interests in China alongside the national security allegations. Nvidia’s advanced chips are a primary target of U.S. efforts to restrict China’s access to AI computing infrastructure . Nvidia’s board accepted Huang’s resignation after reports of two alleged affairs , one involving Alice Huang. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO , and the board launched an independent investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The congressional session could bring three issues under examination at once: Nvidia’s leadership transition, its contacts involving China, and its role in semiconductor export policy. sources.title: Google's latest Search upgrade promises better answers to your most complicated questions - TechCrunch
passages: Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos.
The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.”

In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode.
In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly.
Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says.
Google says the Hydrogen update is rolling out to all Search users globally.
The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do.
Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries.
This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains.

extraction.body: Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.” While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement. The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, its previous fast model, but it’s still pretty smart, even beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on one broad intelligence benchmark, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index , at its default high thinking level. In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode. In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question. Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains. The addition of Hydrogen to Search will also mean more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools will appear as visual responses to users’ queries in AI Mode. Google also says Hydrogen can work on its own for everyday work in areas like writing code, running tests, or verifying code changes, or it can be paired with Carbon and Argon in workflows that combine several models. The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new, extra-high tier (“xhigh”), all of which are designed to complete tasks faster with fewer output tokens. On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks, the company pointed out. In addition to Search, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is coming to all tiers of Google’s AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini App, and the paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google’s Antigravity development platform. Google says the Hydrogen update is rolling out to all Search users globally. And to make those answers more relevant, Google is also improving how Search gathers information from the web.
It can break down complicated questions into smaller searches, explore different aspects at once, and find relevant information from a wider range of websites.
That means you could find helpful sources that wouldn’t necessarily appear in your usual searches.

Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries.

extraction.body: Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.” While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement. The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, its previous fast model, but it’s still pretty smart, even beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on one broad intelligence benchmark, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index , at its default high thinking level. In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode. In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question. Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains. The addition of Hydrogen to Search will also mean more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools will appear as visual responses to users’ queries in AI Mode. Google also says Hydrogen can work on its own for everyday work in areas like writing code, running tests, or verifying code changes, or it can be paired with Carbon and Argon in workflows that combine several models. The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new, extra-high tier (“xhigh”), all of which are designed to complete tasks faster with fewer output tokens. On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks, the company pointed out. In addition to Search, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is coming to all tiers of Google’s AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini App, and the paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google’s Antigravity development platform. passages: Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.”

While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement.

The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, its previous fast model, but it’s still pretty smart, even beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on one broad intelligence benchmark, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index , at its default high thinking level.

In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode.

In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question.

Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains.
The addition of Hydrogen to Search will also mean more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools will appear as visual responses to users’ queries in AI Mode.

Google also says Hydrogen can work on its own for everyday work in areas like writing code, running tests, or verifying code changes, or it can be paired with Carbon and Argon in workflows that combine several models.
The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new, extra-high tier (“xhigh”), all of which are designed to complete tasks faster with fewer output tokens.
On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks, the company pointed out.

In addition to Search, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is coming to all tiers of Google’s AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini App, and the paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google’s Antigravity development platform.

sources.title: Here are the 3 Android XR smart glasses announcements I’m hoping to see tomorrow at Google I/O 2026 - TechRadar
passages: Google I/O is less than a day away, and the annual software showcase would be the perfect opportunity for Google and its partners to showcase their 2026 Android XR tech: the XR glasses we’ve been promised will land this year.
So from Xreal and Samsung , to Gucci and Gentle Monster, here are the three smart glasses announcements we’ll hopefully see on May 19 — and why you should get excited.
I love Xreal’s specs, and have done for a while — if you want a pair of XR glasses you’ll struggle to beat the Xreal One Pros .

Now, leaks and rumors suggest the display model won’t actually land until 2027 but I expect they'll get some time in the spotlight if the displayless specs are shown off — in part to build excitement and prove Android XR has a long term plan (to rebut fears this is Google Glass 2.0), and in part to make Samsung not appear too far behind Meta’s technology (as its Ray-ban Display specs are already available to buy in the US).
But with Google taking a software-centric approach — letting others handle the hardware — it makes sense that this new generation of smart glasses would land at a software show like I/O.
Based on my experience with Ray-Ban smart glasses, AI assistance can be super handy, especially as a tourist.
Where Aura improves on the current design is it includes cameras by default for hand and object tracking.
It's a bit more basic than the Samsung Galaxy XR headset's system as Xreal lacks eye tracking, but it should make your Android XR experiences feel more interactive than Xreal's previous tech.

Though his specialty is writing about everything going on in the world of virtual reality and augmented reality.

This matches Xreal’s XR approach with previous models and offers some design advantages, but also some constraints. This approach might not be as mobile as the Ray-Ban and Samsung AI or AR specs, but should be a lot more capable where it counts.The glasses virtually project a giant display in front of your face, like your own private cinema, and boast the same superb optics as the Xreal One (so expect excellent OLED contrast and colors, a wide field of view, and fewer disruptive reflections in the lenses compared with rivals on the market). Whether you want a virtual display for working across multiple windows at once, or an immersive portable cinema for your face the Xreal One pro are the glasses to get because of these optics. Where Aura improves on the current design is it includes cameras by default for hand and object tracking. It's a bit more basic than the Samsung Galaxy XR headset's system as Xreal lacks eye tracking, but it should make your Android XR experiences feel more interactive than Xreal's previous tech. The issue is I expect these specs will be pricey. The Xreal One Pros launched at $649, with a camera Xreal Eye add-on costing $99. The puck is also reminiscent of the Beam Pro and is likely to add a couple hundred to the price meaning we might be lucky if Xreal's Aura comes in under $1,000. Even though I believe Samsung will focus on its own launch event — perhaps tying its smart glasses release into its annual foldables event, which typically takes place in a few months — there’s a chance it’ll instead debut its glasses at I/O. Not just one pair at that, we might get to see two. The first would be a more standard AI-focused design with a camera, speakers, and microphones, but no display, just like the basic (but impressive) Ray-Ban Meta specs. Speaking of, the design recently leaked, and they do look strikingly similar to the Ray-Ban model. The only difference we know so far is they'll rely on Gemini instead of Meta AI, which is generally agreed to be a more capable assistant, and has better interoperability between the core Android apps for more personalized contextual responses. With a better understanding of my schedule through my calendar, or the context of the photos I've taken with my phone, I'm hoping the Gemini-powered specs might offer better day-to-day usefulness. Best of all, Samsung’s specs should be fairly affordable too. These smart glasses are rumored to cost between $379 and $499, which puts them roughly inline with Meta's pricing — though we’ll have to wait and see what Samsung announces to know for sure, pricing has been all over thanks to various global economic challenges. As for Samsung’s second pair of specs, they would be practically the same, but with a display. Now, leaks and rumors suggest the display model won’t actually land until 2027 but I expect they'll get some time in the spotlight if the displayless specs are shown off — in part to build excitement and prove Android XR has a long term plan (to rebut fears this is Google Glass 2.0), and in part to make Samsung not appear too far behind Meta’s technology (as its Ray-ban Display specs are already available to buy in the US). It's frustrating that we might have to wait a little longer for these display glasses, though, seeing the supply issues Meta has had with its version, and the high price tag, Samsung's delay might mean it can bring us a more reliably available and affordable version of this exciting emerging tech. Lastly, my bold Google I/O prediction: we’ll get an XR fashion show with models strutting down the runway in Gucci, Gentle Monster, and Warby Parker smart specs. Much like how Meta has partnered with EssilorLuxottica’s Oakley and Ray-Ban, Android XR companies are partnering with fashion brands to bring some style to their specs. Given how much glasses can play into someone’s visual identity, a fashion focus is key, and offering a variety of looks is key to capturing different users and use cases — just look at Meta, its Ray-Bans are superb for everyday wear and casual vacationing, while its Oakleys are perfect for athletes. With a wider variety of brands and, hopefully, styles under its belt, Android XR seems to have an advantage over Meta again, and a fashion show moment would be the perfect way to highlight the variety it’s set to offer. Plus, Google has shown it isn’t afraid to mix things up with its events — last year, the Made by Google Pixel 10 launch show was hosted by Jimmy Fallon and featured a large cast of celebrities and segments that felt more like a variety show than a technology keynote. So I’m hoping we might see some fun smart-glasses showcases, though I’ll admit my fashion-show pitch might be a little out there — and it assumes Google, Gentle Monster, Gucci, and Warby Parker are even ready to showcase their designs. passages: Google and Samsung are leveraging Warby Parker and Gentle Monster's brick-and-mortar presence and retail expertise, which lets people demo the glasses before buying them. (Kering Eyewear, which owns brands like Lindberg and Maui Jim, has also signed up to make glasses for Android XR in the future.) The first models are available for preorder now, with official sales starting on December 10.
The “Intelligent Eyewear” is a collaboration between the two tech companies, with Samsung providing its hardware expertise and Google handling much of the software platform.
You're not talking to Google, you're talking to Gemini.” Oddly, these glasses are only compatible with certain devices—Google Pixel phones, Samsung Galaxy phones, and iPhones—and only select models.
Still, the new spoken wake phrase distinguishes the glasses as Gemini's “optimal form,” according to Juston Payne, Google's senior director of product management for XR.
You'll need a Pixel 7 or newer, Galaxy S or Z Fold running Samsung's One UI 9.0 or higher, and the iPhone 13 Pro or newer.

As for plans to launch audio-only smart glasses, like Meta's recent Ray-Ban Audio, Warby Parker co-CEO Dave Gilboa tells WIRED, “There's a pretty robust pipeline of additional products.” What Can They Do?

That's likely because Meta has faced public scrutiny over how people use its smart glasses, so much so that it has spawned a new term for people wearing them: the Meta Creep (harkening back to when anyone wearing Google Glasses was called a “Glasshole”).
Google has already previewed Intelligent Eyewear glasses with displays built into the lenses—useful for showing navigation instructions or real-time captions for folks with hearing issues.
To that end, Google is announcing a series of policies and features alongside the glasses to assuage concerns.
We've highlighted all of Google's privacy-focused announcements around its glasses in a separate story.

Warby Parker's frames start at $395 and come in three styles—Alden, Reid, and Wren—as optical or sunglasses, with various prescription, lens, and width options. Gentle Monster's glasses start at $449 and come in six designs, various colors, and tints, with prescription options for most frames. The glasses weigh around 41 grams (10 grams less than Meta's new Gen 3 glasses), have a nine-hour battery life, and include a charging case that can recharge the glasses up to seven times. A touch-sensitive temple piece lets you tap to activate the onboard Gemini assistant, or slide two fingers back and forth to control the volume of the audio coming out of the glasses' speaker. They are the first devices to support the “Hey Gemini” hotword, though you can use the well-known “Hey Google” hotword if you'd like. You'll need a Pixel 7 or newer, Galaxy S or Z Fold running Samsung's One UI 9.0 or higher, and the iPhone 13 Pro or newer. A Google spokesperson tells WIRED the company will share more about how it plans to expand support to other phones in 2027 after launch. Since you'll be buying the glasses from an eyewear brand, they will be the customer-facing party to handle any problems you may have with the device or prescriptions. Google has already previewed Intelligent Eyewear glasses with displays built into the lenses—useful for showing navigation instructions or real-time captions for folks with hearing issues. However, they are not ready yet; Payne says they're currently being tested by “non-Googlers” and are still on the road map, though he didn't share a specific release window. As for plans to launch audio-only smart glasses, like Meta's recent Ray-Ban Audio, Warby Parker co-CEO Dave Gilboa tells WIRED, “There's a pretty robust pipeline of additional products.” What Can They Do? Unlike display smart glasses designed to plug into a laptop to mirror or extend your screen, or more immersive glasses like Meta's VR Glasses, which layer virtual experiences over the real world, Intelligent Eyewear is more akin to what Google pitched years ago with the original Google Glass. You can listen to music, take phone calls, and get audio navigation through Google Maps. Yes, you can snap photos and videos too, though Payne quickly notes that these glasses are designed more to have Gemini assist you throughout the day than to capture content. That's likely because Meta has faced public scrutiny over how people use its smart glasses, so much so that it has spawned a new term for people wearing them: the Meta Creep (harkening back to when anyone wearing Google Glasses was called a “Glasshole”). “We learned through Glass that you can make people uncomfortable if you're not clearly communicating,” Payne says. When you ask Gemini to look at something, those visuals are not saved in your Gemini History, and Google says it will not use them to train AI models or target ads. The glasses will automatically redact the faces of people around you before Gemini processes the visual data. We've highlighted all of Google's privacy-focused announcements around its glasses in a separate story. Most of the features that Google is positioning around Intelligent Eyewear rely on Gemini. Google is also collaborating with Aira so you can stream the glasses' feed straight to a human interpreter for real-time visual support. To help demystify these features—and convince consumers that smart glasses aren't just a fad for tech bros—Warby Parker and Gentle Monster are both launching pop-up experiences in New York City this week. Gentle Monster's pop-up will run for about a month, but Warby Parker's “Literatureland” will be open through 2027, letting people walk through the experience with a pair of nonprescription glasses to demo Gemini's capabilities. “These are the original wearables that have been around for hundreds of years,” Warby Parker's Gilboa says.

extraction.body: The Xreal Aura, spatial computing glasses made in partnership with Google for the Android XR platform, are now available to order. We first learned about these XR glasses at Google I/O 2026, and early adopters can finally try them in a matter of weeks. The futuristic XR device combines elements of augmented reality and virtual reality in a pair of smart glasses. They're the first wired smart glasses to run on the new Android XR operating system from Google. The glasses and accessories are available for preorder at the Xreal website as of today, and they're scheduled to ship in mid-November, according to a press release shared with Mashable. Customers who preorder the glasses can save $180 on the hefty $1,279 price tag.“Xreal Aura is finally here, and we're so proud to unlock new ways for people to work, watch, play, and build," said Chi Xu, co-founder and CEO of XREAL, in a press release.The Xreal Aura utilizes dual Sony Micro-OLED displays to create a virtual display with a 70-degree field of view, up to 1,050 nits of brightness, and up to a 120Hz refresh rate. Credit: Xreal Credit: Xreal Xreal is one of the leading augmented reality companies, known for its tethered AR glasses, which project a large virtual display into the user's field of view. The Xreal Aura will provide spatial computing and virtual reality experiences usually associated with headsets in the smart glasses form factor.The Xreal Aura is part of a new generation of spatial computing smart glasses, along with the Specs AR glasses from Snap and the recently announced Meta VR glasses. The Meta VR glasses have a $1,299 price tag but won't launch until spring 2027.What do the Xreal Aura Glasses do? Credit: Xreal / Mashable Photo Composite Xreal says the new glasses will support "productivity, immersive entertainment, and next-generation XR experiences."The Xreal Aura offer the same augmented reality features as other AR smart glasses, but they up the ante with spatial computing experiences powered by the Android XR operating system and Qualcomm's Snapdragon Reality Elite Platform. (A press release states that the glasses were made in partnership with Google and Qualcomm.) Unlike most AR glasses, the Xreal Aura can also be controlled via voice and hand movements, thanks to onboard sensors and cameras. Instead of simply plugging into a user's smartphone, laptop, or gaming device, the Aura glasses come with a puck, which houses the battery and powers most of the compute necessary for spatial computing.The Apple Vision Pro introduced spatial computing into the public consciousness. The technology turns a user's surroundings into a 360-degree virtual canvas, and users can open apps, games, entertainment, and AI tools directly into their space. However, unlike headsets, which can be extremely limiting, smart glasses don't limit a user's movements or block their peripheral vision. “This is a defining moment for XR," Xu said in a press release. "We built AURA for people who want the power of spatial computing without being removed from the world around them. With transparent lenses, a category-leading lightweight design, Gemini by your side, and access to the Android ecosystem from day-one, the promise of XR is more approachable than ever."The Xreal Aura will also offer support for Gemini, letting users ask questions about their environment or complete tasks across apps.Spatial photos, virtual reality, and more Credit: Xreal / Android XR Using Google Photos and Android XR, Aura users will be able to view their photos and videos in new immersive ways. Via Google Maps, users can explore destinations in immersive 3D, either with an aerial view or via Street View.Users can also enjoy 360-degree and VR180 video content on YouTube.New XR experiencesAt launch, users will also be able to access a library of more than 150 XR experiences, with more to come in the months ahead. Some of the highlights include:NBA App for Android XRFallout: Factions video gameProject Hail Mary: Journey Among the Stars, a mixed-reality adventure NASCAR XR appOh My Galaxy!, a physics-based arcade gameXR HoloMedicineSimply Piano XRWhere to preorder the Xreal AuraThe Xreal Aura are available for preorder now exclusively at the Xreal online store. The glasses have a retail price of $1,279 but are available for $1,099 for a limited time.

coreStoryFacts.text: Google I/O is less than a day away, and the annual software showcase would be the perfect opportunity for Google and its partners to showcase their 2026 Android XR tech: the XR glasses we’ve been promised will land this year.
So from Xreal and Samsung , to Gucci and Gentle Monster, here are the three smart glasses announcements we’ll hopefully see on May 19 — and why you should get excited.
I love Xreal’s specs, and have done for a while — if you want a pair of XR glasses you’ll struggle to beat the Xreal One Pros .

Now, leaks and rumors suggest the display model won’t actually land until 2027 but I expect they'll get some time in the spotlight if the displayless specs are shown off — in part to build excitement and prove Android XR has a long term plan (to rebut fears this is Google Glass 2.0), and in part to make Samsung not appear too far behind Meta’s technology (as its Ray-ban Display specs are already available to buy in the US).
But with Google taking a software-centric approach — letting others handle the hardware — it makes sense that this new generation of smart glasses would land at a software show like I/O.
Based on my experience with Ray-Ban smart glasses, AI assistance can be super handy, especially as a tourist.
Where Aura improves on the current design is it includes cameras by default for hand and object tracking.
It's a bit more basic than the Samsung Galaxy XR headset's system as Xreal lacks eye tracking, but it should make your Android XR experiences feel more interactive than Xreal's previous tech.

It's frustrating that we might have to wait a little longer for these display glasses, though, seeing the supply issues Meta has had with its version, and the high price tag, Samsung's delay might mean it can bring us a more reliably available and affordable version of this exciting emerging tech.
A video Google showed off yesterday revealed that Gemini on Android XR smart glasses can remember things, such as where you left a specific object.
Other demos include asking the chatbot how to operate a coffee machine as well as looking at a record and asking Gemini to play a track from it.
Wired reports that there’s indeed no firm window for these glasses.
Meanwhile, Android ecosystem lead Sameer Samat told Bloomberg that the company would launch Android XR glasses “when it makes sense.”
Google just announced Android XR , with a Samsung-produced headset being the first product to run the new platform.

Google I/O is less than a day away, and the annual software showcase would be the perfect opportunity for Google and its partners to showcase their 2026 Android XR tech: the XR glasses we’ve been promised will land this year. Google isn’t a stranger to smart specs, but since the rapid rise and fall of Google Glass, we’ve seen the likes of the Ray-Ban Meta glasses take the smart specs world by storm, and now the old king wants his crown back. But with Google taking a software-centric approach — letting others handle the hardware — it makes sense that this new generation of smart glasses would land at a software show like I/O. So from Xreal and Samsung , to Gucci and Gentle Monster, here are the three smart glasses announcements we’ll hopefully see on May 19 — and why you should get excited. I love Xreal’s specs, and have done for a while — if you want a pair of XR glasses you’ll struggle to beat the Xreal One Pros . So I’m especially excited to see the final version of its Project Aura Android XR glasses, and they’re also the pair we’re most likely to find at Google I/O (because unlike Samsung, Xreal doesn’t have a high profile tech events of its own in the calendar). The big difference between Xreal’s Aura glasses and some other AI smart glasses we’ve been seeing is they’ll be wired. This matches Xreal’s XR approach with previous models and offers some design advantages, but also some constraints. With no internal battery the Project Aura glasses should feel lighter and less bulky, but they’ll need to run from a connected device (in Aura’s case that’s a dedicated compute puck that doubles as a trackpad and a battery pack) plus they’ll be best suited to stationary activities (working, and watching TV) rather than using them on the move. This approach might not be as mobile as the Ray-Ban and Samsung AI or AR specs, but should be a lot more capable where it counts.The glasses virtually project a giant display in front of your face, like your own private cinema, and boast the same superb optics as the Xreal One (so expect excellent OLED contrast and colors, a wide field of view, and fewer disruptive reflections in the lenses compared with rivals on the market). Whether you want a virtual display for working across multiple windows at once, or an immersive portable cinema for your face the Xreal One pro are the glasses to get because of these optics. Where Aura improves on the current design is it includes cameras by default for hand and object tracking. It's a bit more basic than the Samsung Galaxy XR headset's system as Xreal lacks eye tracking, but it should make your Android XR experiences feel more interactive than Xreal's previous tech. The issue is I expect these specs will be pricey. The Xreal One Pros launched at $649, with a camera Xreal Eye add-on costing $99. The puck is also reminiscent of the Beam Pro and is likely to add a couple hundred to the price meaning we might be lucky if Xreal's Aura comes in under $1,000. Even though I believe Samsung will focus on its own launch event — perhaps tying its smart glasses release into its annual foldables event, which typically takes place in a few months — there’s a chance it’ll instead debut its glasses at I/O. Not just one pair at that, we might get to see two. The first would be a more standard AI-focused design with a camera, speakers, and microphones, but no display, just like the basic (but impressive) Ray-Ban Meta specs. Speaking of, the design recently leaked, and they do look strikingly similar to the Ray-Ban model. The only difference we know so far is they'll rely on Gemini instead of Meta AI, which is generally agreed to be a more capable assistant, and has better interoperability between the core Android apps for more personalized contextual responses. Based on my experience with Ray-Ban smart glasses, AI assistance can be super handy, especially as a tourist. With a better understanding of my schedule through my calendar, or the context of the photos I've taken with my phone, I'm hoping the Gemini-powered specs might offer better day-to-day usefulness. Best of all, Samsung’s specs should be fairly affordable too. These smart glasses are rumored to cost between $379 and $499, which puts them roughly inline with Meta's pricing — though we’ll have to wait and see what Samsung announces to know for sure, pricing has been all over thanks to various global economic challenges. As for Samsung’s second pair of specs, they would be practically the same, but with a display. Now, leaks and rumors suggest the display model won’t actually land until 2027 but I expect they'll get some time in the spotlight if the displayless specs are shown off — in part to build excitement and prove Android XR has a long term plan (to rebut fears this is Google Glass 2.0), and in part to make Samsung not appear too far behind Meta’s technology (as its Ray-ban Display specs are already available to buy in the US). It's frustrating that we might have to wait a little longer for these display glasses, though, seeing the supply issues Meta has had with its version, and the high price tag, Samsung's delay might mean it can bring us a more reliably available and affordable version of this exciting emerging tech. Lastly, my bold Google I/O prediction: we’ll get an XR fashion show with models strutting down the runway in Gucci, Gentle Monster, and Warby Parker smart specs. Much like how Meta has partnered with EssilorLuxottica’s Oakley and Ray-Ban, Android XR companies are partnering with fashion brands to bring some style to their specs. Given how much glasses can play into someone’s visual identity, a fashion focus is key, and offering a variety of looks is key to capturing different users and use cases — just look at Meta, its Ray-Bans are superb for everyday wear and casual vacationing, while its Oakleys are perfect for athletes. With a wider variety of brands and, hopefully, styles under its belt, Android XR seems to have an advantage over Meta again, and a fashion show moment would be the perfect way to highlight the variety it’s set to offer. Plus, Google has shown it isn’t afraid to mix things up with its events — last year, the Made by Google Pixel 10 launch show was hosted by Jimmy Fallon and featured a large cast of celebrities and segments that felt more like a variety show than a technology keynote. So I’m hoping we might see some fun smart-glasses showcases, though I’ll admit my fashion-show pitch might be a little out there — and it assumes Google, Gentle Monster, Gucci, and Warby Parker are even ready to showcase their designs. Other demos include asking the chatbot how to operate a coffee machine as well as looking at a record and asking Gemini to play a track from it.
Wired reports that there’s indeed no firm window for these glasses.
Meanwhile, Android ecosystem lead Sameer Samat told Bloomberg that the company would launch Android XR glasses “when it makes sense.”
Google just announced Android XR , with a Samsung-produced headset being the first product to run the new platform.
The company also confirmed that smart glasses were coming later , and we now have a better idea of how these glasses will work.
Will these glasses be made by Google, Samsung, or someone else?
However, Google said it would soon distribute these prototype glasses to a “small group of users” as part of a real-world testing program.
However, your notifications are summarized with AI to reduce the amount of text in your vision.
You can then respond to these notifications via Gemini.
You can also take pictures by tapping the right arm, complete with previews after capturing to ensure you got the best snap.
Thankfully, Google promised a brighter, more vivid picture down the line.
It wouldn’t be the first time Google launched its own smart glasses, though.
The company previously launched its pioneering Google Glass spectacles in the early 2010s, although these never gained widespread adoption.
These spectacles incorporated a camera and voice commands too.
But between chatbot advancements, more advanced processors, and new battery technology, the landscape has changed significantly since then.
Most of the processing is handled by a paired smartphone, and Google is apparently aiming for ” all-day” battery life as a result.
It’s unclear how many features will be available without a paired phone.

Fingers crossed that we see options without a display as that would likely be much cheaper and offer better battery life.
