coreStoryFacts.text: U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security.
This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.
Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.
The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday.

Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him.
Nvidia, Huang, and Powell have not confirmed the report.
Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said .
The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress , will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties.

The chairmen of the House Select Committee on China, the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and the House Intelligence Committee formally requested a closed-door briefing from Jensen Huang, with the request reported around November 5, 2026.
No public response from Huang or Nvidia was identified in the cited reporting at that time.
During 2024 and into 2025 , media reports said Jensen Huang and Alice Huang were photographed or observed socializing in Taiwan, where Jensen Huang was born.
The memo allegedly stated she had been recruited to gather information about Jensen Huang .
It also alleged she was tasked with influencing Nvidia’s commercial position on advanced chip sales to China.
Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led it since.
Alice Huang , also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese citizen and former senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data-center company that rents computing capacity built on Nvidia processors.
Nvidia responded by characterizing Jensen Huang’s interactions with her as ordinary customer-related contact.

Public reporting has not established what information Alice Huang allegedly obtained, whether any Nvidia proprietary information was transferred, or whether export-control violations involving Megaspeed occurred.

Congressional committees have requested access to Jensen Huang ; no hearing date has been announced, and until investigators publish conclusions or authorities bring formal charges, the espionage allegations remain unproven.

In October 2025 , U.S. and Singapore authorities reportedly examined whether Megaspeed had helped Chinese firms, including Alibaba, obtain Nvidia processors in potential violation of U.S. export restrictions.

WASHINGTON (TNND) — In a stunning development, Nvidia announced Thursday that Jensen Huang had resigned from the company he helped found in 1993.
The resignation followed revelations that Huang reportedly had affairs with two women: an executive who reported to him and a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.
According to The Wall Street Journal, in 2023 Alice Huang created 'Megaspeed,' a company seeking to build data centers in Asia using Nvidia chips.

extraction.body: Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security. U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported. The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang, and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities. Nvidia confirmed in an SEC filing on Thursday that the board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress , will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang. Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993. Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26. “Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.” The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed. After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days. Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan. The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO. According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year. Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed . The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum. Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported . The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips. Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported . Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang. In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported. On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO. “I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said. When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia , Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.” Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife. “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.” An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary. “Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.” U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times. Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo. Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service. Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born. These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. facts.text: U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security.
This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.
Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.
The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday.

Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him.
Nvidia, Huang, and Powell have not confirmed the report.
Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said .
The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress , will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties.

The chairmen of the House Select Committee on China, the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and the House Intelligence Committee formally requested a closed-door briefing from Jensen Huang, with the request reported around November 5, 2026.
No public response from Huang or Nvidia was identified in the cited reporting at that time.
During 2024 and into 2025 , media reports said Jensen Huang and Alice Huang were photographed or observed socializing in Taiwan, where Jensen Huang was born.
The memo allegedly stated she had been recruited to gather information about Jensen Huang .
It also alleged she was tasked with influencing Nvidia’s commercial position on advanced chip sales to China.
Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led it since.
Alice Huang , also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese citizen and former senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data-center company that rents computing capacity built on Nvidia processors.
Nvidia responded by characterizing Jensen Huang’s interactions with her as ordinary customer-related contact.

Public reporting has not established what information Alice Huang allegedly obtained, whether any Nvidia proprietary information was transferred, or whether export-control violations involving Megaspeed occurred.

Congressional committees have requested access to Jensen Huang ; no hearing date has been announced, and until investigators publish conclusions or authorities bring formal charges, the espionage allegations remain unproven.

In October 2025 , U.S. and Singapore authorities reportedly examined whether Megaspeed had helped Chinese firms, including Alibaba, obtain Nvidia processors in potential violation of U.S. export restrictions.

Microsoft hasn’t given a specific cause, but said that it was providing updates in its admin center , which wasn’t reachable at the time of publication.
In its latest update, Microsoft attributed this incident to “a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable,” for reasons it did not explain.
Microsoft said it continues to investigate the outage.
Microsoft says its video conferencing tool Teams, file sharing platform SharePoint, and its AI tool Copilot are also unavailable.
The company says its Defender XDR security system is also affected by the outage.
Consumers are also unable to access their OneDrive storage, Office (for the web), and several other Microsoft services during the ongoing outage.
TechCrunch will reach out to Microsoft for comment, as soon as our own email service has resumed.

Eastern Time.AP also reported more than 46,000 complaints involving Microsoft 365 and approximately 3,000 reports concerning Microsoft Teams.The disruption was not limited to Outlook.
Other services, including SharePoint Online, Microsoft Copilot 365 and Microsoft Defender XDR, were also identified as potentially affected.

However, this does not mean that all users experienced difficulties across every application.As part of its recovery efforts, Microsoft had already redistributed connection traffic across its worldwide infrastructure and moved additional traffic away from affected systems to reduce the pressure.

The company was also restarting affected servers and investigating the reasons behind their unexpected unavailability.The latest clarification shifts the focus of the investigation towards server availability and infrastructure reliability, rather than unusually high user demand.Microsoft has not yet publicly identified the underlying reason why the servers became unavailable in the update.

coreStoryFacts.text: The company’s last major incident was in September , when a days-long outage hit Microsoft 365, its online productivity suite that includes Outlook.
During that outage, Microsoft blamed a “core authentication configuration” issue that prevented users from accessing the service.
Microsoft hasn’t given a specific cause, but said that it was providing updates in its admin center , which wasn’t reachable at the time of publication.
In its latest update, Microsoft attributed this incident to “a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable,” for reasons it did not explain.
Microsoft said it continues to investigate the outage.
Microsoft says its video conferencing tool Teams, file sharing platform SharePoint, and its AI tool Copilot are also unavailable.
The company says its Defender XDR security system is also affected by the outage.
Consumers are also unable to access their OneDrive storage, Office (for the web), and several other Microsoft services during the ongoing outage.
TechCrunch will reach out to Microsoft for comment, as soon as our own email service has resumed.
More than 130,000 incident reports were submitted to Downdetector during the outage , though that figure measures submitted reports rather than a confirmed count of distinct affected users.
The scale of those reports still signals a substantial network disruption hitting Outlook and Exchange Online users in multiple regions at once.
If your organization's tenant is affected, you may experience interruptions across email workflows, calendar access, authentication processes, and collaboration tools.
Users are reporting inability to open Outlook, send or receive email, or hold a stable connection to their mailbox.

Microsoft 365 services separately confirmed it resolved an earlier Teams disruption affecting users in North America, but broader Microsoft 365 connectivity problems remain active and are separate from that resolved incident.
Hold off on resetting passwords or rebuilding Outlook profiles until you have confirmed what Microsoft's incident updates say.
Microsoft has identified potential impact beyond email, though the full scope of affected services remains under evaluation.

US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim. Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software. According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet. Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call – except that the audio would appear to malfunction. A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims. Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities. The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user". "It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday. "If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough." extraction.body: WASHINGTON - North Korean state-sponsored hackers have stolen more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the last 18 months by misusing secretly recorded webcam videos, the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation said Thursday. The FBI said the group employed an artificial intelligence-assisted social engineering scheme called FaceStealer, in which imposters use such webcam videos to deceive others on video conference platforms. The FBI said the hackers also turned to AI to create deepfake videos of well-known and influential individuals and used them to gain the trust of targeted individuals during online meetings. The FBI has disrupted cloud-based infrastructure used in the scheme and seized over 900 webcam videos of victims across the world, it said, warning that anyone who owns cryptocurrency or works in the industry could be a target. "The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program," FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman said in a statement. "The FBI remains committed to identifying, disrupting, and imposing cost on North Korean actors targeting the virtual asset community," he added. North Korea has also been accused of involvement in a massive theft of virtual assets from the Binance cryptocurrency exchange platform in late October. The FBI said a group known as TraderTraitor was behind the more than $6 billion heist. North Korea has denied the U.S. allegation as "absurd rhetoric," with Kim Yo Jong, the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, describing it as an attempt to brand North Korea as a "cyber criminal state" and a "grave political provocation" against her country.

US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim. Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software. According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet. Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call – except that the audio would appear to malfunction. A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims. Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities. The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user". "It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday. "If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough." extraction.body: WASHINGTON - North Korean state-sponsored hackers have stolen more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the last 18 months by misusing secretly recorded webcam videos, the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation said Thursday. The FBI said the group employed an artificial intelligence-assisted social engineering scheme called FaceStealer, in which imposters use such webcam videos to deceive others on video conference platforms. The FBI said the hackers also turned to AI to create deepfake videos of well-known and influential individuals and used them to gain the trust of targeted individuals during online meetings. The FBI has disrupted cloud-based infrastructure used in the scheme and seized over 900 webcam videos of victims across the world, it said, warning that anyone who owns cryptocurrency or works in the industry could be a target. "The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program," FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman said in a statement. "The FBI remains committed to identifying, disrupting, and imposing cost on North Korean actors targeting the virtual asset community," he added. North Korea has also been accused of involvement in a massive theft of virtual assets from the Binance cryptocurrency exchange platform in late October. The FBI said a group known as TraderTraitor was behind the more than $6 billion heist. North Korea has denied the U.S. allegation as "absurd rhetoric," with Kim Yo Jong, the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, describing it as an attempt to brand North Korea as a "cyber criminal state" and a "grave political provocation" against her country.

extraction.body: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia, after Huang quit over revelations of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. “Now that Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place — TIM COOK of Apple,” Trump said on his Truth Social network. Trump has no formal say in who should run chip giant Nvidia, which is at the center of the AI revolution, but his extraordinary intervention underscores his close ties to both Huang and Cook. During his second presidency, Trump has treated Nvidia co-founder Huang as a close adviser, even bringing him on board Air Force One for a state visit to China in May. After allegations emerged about Huang’s ties to Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, Trump this week defended the Nvidia boss and said he had no idea Alice Huang was allegedly spying for Beijing. Trump added that Jensen Huang, who is not related to Alice Huang, was “suffering greatly” and described the Taiwanese-born tech boss as “an amazing guy.” But Trump still faces questions over what he knew about the allegations — and when he knew. The New York Times reported earlier this week that Trump was informed about the allegations by Secretary of State Marco Rubio aboard Air Force One in May — shortly before picking up Huang in Alaska for the flight to Beijing. Cook — who stood down as Apple CEO in September but remains executive chair of its board of directors — is another of the tech titans who have swarmed around the White House since Trump’s return. In August 2025, Cook appeared in the Oval Office with Trump to announce that Apple would increase its investments in the US to $600 billion, as Trump threatened huge tariffs on tech products made abroad. He also brought one of the flashy presents that Trump loves — a custom-engraved glass piece made by iPhone glassmaker Corning, set in a 24-karat gold base. The gift helped smooth relations between Cook and Trump, who had repeatedly criticized Apple in the past for not manufacturing its iPhones in the United States. Cook also accompanied Trump to China in May, and both he and Huang attended the lavish state banquet that the US president held at the White House for Xi in September.

“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump wrote on Truth Social.
The post was Trump’s first public statement on Huang’s departure. It is unclear whether Trump had approached Cook about the idea and that it had asked the White House for comment.

Earlier on Thursday, Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and board member with immediate effect. Colette Kress, Nvidia’s executive vice-president and chief financial officer, will serve as interim chief executive while the board searches for a permanent successor.

Cook stepped down as Apple’s chief executive on September 1 after 15 years in the role and became executive chairman. The change was announced in April. John Ternus, previously a senior vice-president, succeeded him.

Trump is close to both men. Huang and Cook travelled with Trump on his visit to China in May. In September, they sat at the same table at a White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping. Last year, after Apple said it would invest an additional $100 billion in US manufacturing, Cook gave Trump a custom US-made plaque mounted on a 24-carat gold stand to mark Apple’s “American Manufacturing Program”.

On Wednesday, the newspaper cited five people who had worked at Nvidia and reported a second affair, with an Nvidia executive who reported to Huang.
Huang said he had been unfaithful to his wife. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” he said, according to Bloomberg.

Nvidia’s board started an independent investigation and on Tuesday said it had hired former acting US attorney Joon H. Kim and his firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, to lead it. The board had earlier said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets” were compromised by the relationship. The FBI has also opened an investigation.
Republican lawmakers have asked Huang to attend a joint closed-door briefing on November 18 on Nvidia’s security protocols and his dealings with the alleged spy.

Earlier this week, Trump defended Huang. He said Huang had told him he did not know the woman was allegedly a spy. “I really believe him,” Trump told reporters. “I think that he’ll be in good shape.” He called Huang “an honorable guy”, adding: “I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what is going on.”

The two men have been close since at least 2025. According to the Times, Trump insisted on including Huang in the May delegation to China despite concerns about his relationship with Alice Huang. Over the past two years, Huang has repeatedly voiced support for the administration’s agenda and has been a regular presence in Washington as Nvidia tried to sell advanced chips in China.

coreStoryFacts.text: I think Tim Cook would be a great candidate to run Nvidia.

Shortly after Huang’s resignation was announced today, Trump posted his idea about Cook on Truth Social: “NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple,” Trump said.

But President Donald Trump is already throwing around one person he thinks should take over the chipmaking giant: former Apple CEO Tim Cook, who stepped down from leading the company on September 1st and moved into an executive chairman role.
So it’s very hard to replace him, but I had an idea this morning that I sort of just released: Tim Cook.
Tim Cook took a lot of these brilliant ideas and designs and everything else from Jobs and others, and he made it into one of the great companies of the world in a fairly short period.

Cook is well-known for his ongoing relationship with President Trump, including gifting the president a 24k gold and glass statue last year. (Trump, after Cook announced his transition plan earlier this year, posted a story about having “the head of Apple calling to ‘kiss my ass.’”) During the podcast, Trump said he spoke to Huang yesterday and that Huang is “going through hell”: > Should [Huang] have stepped down? > Well, the big thing is, was the woman a spy, and I don’t know if that’s been determined yet, but if the woman was a spy, yes, if the woman was not a spy, perhaps it would be different. > But I can tell you this.
Jensen Huang resigned this morning as Nvidia’s CEO following reports of affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

Smith’s Straight Shooter podcast published today, Trump made his pitch for Cook again, saying that Apple “would never be what it is today” if Steve Jobs was still “around”: > Can [Huang] be replaced? > Well, you know, the expression, Anybody can be replaced?
Apple and Nvidia didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.
“Now that Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place — TIM COOK of Apple,” Trump said on his Truth Social network.

In August 2025, Cook appeared in the Oval Office with Trump to announce that Apple would increase its investments in the US to $600 billion, as Trump threatened huge tariffs on tech products made abroad.
The gift helped smooth relations between Cook and Trump, who had repeatedly criticized Apple in the past for not manufacturing its iPhones in the United States.
Trump has no formal say in who should run chip giant Nvidia, which is at the center of the AI revolution, but his extraordinary intervention underscores his close ties to both Huang and Cook.
After allegations emerged about Huang’s ties to Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, Trump this week defended the Nvidia boss and said he had no idea Alice Huang was allegedly spying for Beijing.
Cook — who stood down as Apple CEO in September but remains executive chair of its board of directors — is another of the tech titans who have swarmed around the White House since Trump’s return.
During his second presidency, Trump has treated Nvidia co-founder Huang as a close adviser, even bringing him on board Air Force One for a state visit to China in May.
He also brought one of the flashy presents that Trump loves — a custom-engraved glass piece made by iPhone glassmaker Corning, set in a 24-karat gold base.

President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Tim Cook, Apple’s executive chairman and former chief executive, should take over at Nvidia after Jensen Huang resigned from the chipmaker following reports of two extramarital affairs.
A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

Huang resigned after The New York Times reported that he had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), a Singapore-based tech executive whom US intelligence officials suspect of spying for China.
According to the Times , American authorities found that she had illegally smuggled advanced AI chips into China while developing a “close relationship” with Huang.
On Wednesday, the newspaper cited five people who had worked at Nvidia and reported a second affair, with an Nvidia executive who reported to Huang.
The two men have been close since at least 2025.
Over the past two years, Huang has repeatedly voiced support for the administration’s agenda and has been a regular presence in Washington as Nvidia tried to sell advanced chips in China.

President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Tim Cook, Apple’s executive chairman and former chief executive, should take over at Nvidia after Jensen Huang resigned from the chipmaker following reports of two extramarital affairs.
“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump wrote on Truth Social.
The post was Trump’s first public statement on Huang’s departure. It is unclear whether Trump had approached Cook about the idea and that it had asked the White House for comment.

Earlier on Thursday, Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and board member with immediate effect. Colette Kress, Nvidia’s executive vice-president and chief financial officer, will serve as interim chief executive while the board searches for a permanent successor.

Cook stepped down as Apple’s chief executive on September 1 after 15 years in the role and became executive chairman. The change was announced in April. John Ternus, previously a senior vice-president, succeeded him.

Trump is close to both men. Huang and Cook travelled with Trump on his visit to China in May. In September, they sat at the same table at a White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping. Last year, after Apple said it would invest an additional $100 billion in US manufacturing, Cook gave Trump a custom US-made plaque mounted on a 24-carat gold stand to mark Apple’s “American Manufacturing Program”.

Huang resigned after The New York Times reported that he had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), a Singapore-based tech executive whom US intelligence officials suspect of spying for China. According to the Times , American authorities found that she had illegally smuggled advanced AI chips into China while developing a “close relationship” with Huang. On Wednesday, the newspaper cited five people who had worked at Nvidia and reported a second affair, with an Nvidia executive who reported to Huang.
Huang said he had been unfaithful to his wife. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” he said, according to Bloomberg.

Nvidia’s board started an independent investigation and on Tuesday said it had hired former acting US attorney Joon H. Kim and his firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, to lead it. The board had earlier said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets” were compromised by the relationship. The FBI has also opened an investigation.
Republican lawmakers have asked Huang to attend a joint closed-door briefing on November 18 on Nvidia’s security protocols and his dealings with the alleged spy.

Earlier this week, Trump defended Huang. He said Huang had told him he did not know the woman was allegedly a spy. “I really believe him,” Trump told reporters. “I think that he’ll be in good shape.” He called Huang “an honorable guy”, adding: “I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what is going on.”

The two men have been close since at least 2025. According to the Times, Trump insisted on including Huang in the May delegation to China despite concerns about his relationship with Alice Huang. Over the past two years, Huang has repeatedly voiced support for the administration’s agenda and has been a regular presence in Washington as Nvidia tried to sell advanced chips in China.

extraction.body: SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 12 (Reuters) - Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two people familiar with the matter, Reuters has learned. The revelation follows two other extramarital affairs that led to his resignation Thursday. The two women are Alice Huang, who US intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. Reuters is not naming the second employee. Attempts to reach the woman were not successful. Nvidia declined to comment. Powell, Jensen Huang, and a representative for Nvidia's board did not reply to requests for comment. Alice Huang could not be reached for comment. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name. The former Nvidia CEO's decision to resign from the company could disrupt the AI industry that he helped shape. Nvidia has used its financial strength to help create an industry around AI through complex financial arrangements that ease the purchase of the company's chips. It has backed cloud computing companies and AI labs in order to do so. Pressure on Jensen Huang, who is 63 and married, to resign mounted after reports of his affair with Alice Huang. Nvidia's board appointed finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO while it conducts a search to replace Jensen Huang. The board is considering internal and external candidates for the job. Earlier this month, Nvidia's board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time. Shares fell 5.5% on Thursday in active trading. The stock has shed more than 30% of its value since its early October peak. extraction.body: SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 12 (Reuters) - Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two people familiar with the matter, Reuters has learned. The revelation follows two other extramarital affairs that led to his resignation Thursday. The two women are Alice Huang, who US intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. Reuters is not naming the second employee. Attempts to reach the woman were not successful. Nvidia declined to comment. Powell, Jensen Huang, and a representative for Nvidia's board did not reply to requests for comment. Alice Huang could not be reached for comment. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name. The former Nvidia CEO's decision to resign from the company could disrupt the AI industry that he helped shape. Nvidia has used its financial strength to help create an industry around AI through complex financial arrangements that ease the purchase of the company's chips. It has backed cloud computing companies and AI labs in order to do so. Pressure on Jensen Huang, who is 63 and married, to resign mounted after reports of his affair with Alice Huang. Nvidia's board appointed finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO while it conducts a search to replace Jensen Huang. The board is considering internal and external candidates for the job. Earlier this month, Nvidia's board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time. Shares fell 5.5% on Thursday in active trading. The stock has shed more than 30% of its value since its early October peak. (Reporting by Deepa Seetharaman in San Francisco; editing by Kenneth Li and David Gaffen) Copyright Reuters or USA Today via Reuters Connect This story was originally published November 12, 2026 at 2:43 PM .

extraction.body: United Airlines said Wednesday it will stop personal AI assistants and agents from completing ticket bookings on its systems, citing data privacy risks and federal rules the airline says automated agents cannot satisfy. The Wall Street Journal reports that United said the AI tools risk exposing sensitive customer information and could trigger purchases customers didn’t intend to make. The airline also pointed to a legal problem: Federal Aviation Administration and Transportation Department rules require airlines to present certain information to customers directly, something an automated agent can’t always do. United gave one example: an AI agent cannot attest during check-in that a passenger’s bags don’t contain explosives. Under the new policy, AI agents including Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots will still be able to pull up United’s flight options and prices for a customer. What they won’t be able to do is finish the transaction on United’s website. United said its back-end technology can already tell whether a booking came from an individual, a traditional travel agency, or an AI agent, and that for now, it isn’t seeing many bookings coming through AI agents at all. The airline said it will keep evaluating the tools as personal AI assistants evolve. United joins Amazon in keeping purchasing bots at arm’s length, a more cautious stance than other major U.S. carriers have taken. None have publicly moved against AI agents. Southwest Airlines launched a ChatGPT plug-in earlier this year that lets customers search its flight inventory through the chatbot. Delta said AI assistants can complete bookings once authenticated, with extra safeguards applied to “sensitive transactions” such as trips booked for unaccompanied minors. American Airlines said some AI agents, including Muse, can already buy tickets through certain partners, and that customers can direct an AI agent to complete a booking directly on American’s website. United CEO Scott Kirby addressed the company’s approach Tuesday at an event in Chicago. “To be honest, I don’t want to create another middleman,” he said. Kirby said he came to appreciate AI’s potential after building his own sports betting app by vibe-coding it, a process that took three hourly sessions with a tutor. United also issued a broader call to other companies: “consider measures that preserve the data and security of their customers and strengthen safety.” The announcement comes as interest in AI-driven travel booking picks up elsewhere in the industry. OpenAI this week purchased Odessia, a startup building AI tools for booking travel. Last month, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said travel planning ranks among the top use cases for the company’s Muse agent. Companies are racing to build out AI booking capabilities, but actual usage so far looks thin. Uber Technologies said that during the busy Halloween week earlier this month, its drivers completed 320 million trips combined across Uber and Uber Eats. Of those, AI agents accounted for just 500 Uber Eats orders and four ride bookings. AI presents potential beneficial uses for businesses of all sizes as well as individuals. passages: The idea of letting an AI assistant handle everything from finding flights to completing the booking has been gaining traction with AI developers and consumers alike, but not every business in the travel industry is on board with it.One of the biggest names in American aviation, United Airlines, has just drawn a firm line.United Airlines to Block AI Agents From Booking FlightsUnited Airlines has announced it is updating its ticketing policies to restrict AI agents from booking flights through its website, third-party travel agencies, and flight aggregators.

Businesses like United, JPMorgan Chase, and Amazon have moved to block agents over concerns ranging from security and fraud to regulatory compliance and the loss of direct customer relationships.At the same time, other companies including Southwest Airlines are actively building integrations that invite agents into their booking flows.The adoption rate among consumers is still modest: Uber reported that during the week of Halloween 2026, its 320 million trips and deliveries included only 500 AI-agent-driven Uber Eats orders and four rides, suggesting that agentic commerce remains a niche use case despite significant industry attention.

"To be honest, I do not want to create another middleman," Kirby said, articulating a concern that AI agents sitting between United and its customers could erode the direct relationship the airline has built through its own app, website, and loyalty program.Transportation Department, FAA Also Against AI AgentsBeyond United's own business concerns, the airline specifically cited existing federal regulations from the Department of Transportation and the Federal Aviation Administration as reasons why AI agent bookings raise compliance problems that go beyond corporate preference, said Engadget.The FAA and DOT have regulations governing the interaction between airlines and passengers during the booking and check-in process, some of which explicitly require a human acknowledgment or disclosure.

Southwest Airlines took the opposite approach on October 6 when it announced the launch of a first-of-its-kind US airline plugin in ChatGPT, allowing travelers to discover and shop for Southwest flights directly through the AI assistant.Southwest described the plugin as the first step in a phased AI-powered booking approach developed in partnership with OpenAI and Amazon Web Services.

For businesses receiving agent-driven traffic, the concerns center on security, liability, and the dilution of direct consumer relationships.How Do AI Agents Affect the Industry?The question of how AI agents interact with commerce and service businesses is unresolved and playing out in real time across multiple industries simultaneously.

The experience is designed to let travelers move from inspiration and discovery into booking options with Southwest from within a ChatGPT conversation, reducing the number of steps between deciding to travel and completing a purchase."Customers are evolving how they plan their travel, and Southwest is helping to shape what comes next," said Sabrina Callahan, Chief Digital and Marketing Officer at Southwest Airlines.

The plugin is built to allow Southwest to appear earlier in the customer journey and offer a more direct path from intent to booking, with the airline viewing the AI-assisted channel as a way to reach customers where they are already searching.The difference in approach between United and Southwest illustrates that there is no industry-wide consensus on how to handle agentic commerce in travel.

United operates a hub-and-spoke network with hubs at major airports including Chicago O'Hare, Newark Liberty, Houston George Bush Intercontinental, Denver International, Los Angeles International, San Francisco International, and Washington Dulles.The airline is a founding member of the Star Alliance, the world's largest global airline alliance.

extraction.body: United Airlines said Wednesday it will stop personal AI assistants and agents from completing ticket bookings on its systems, citing data privacy risks and federal rules the airline says automated agents cannot satisfy. The Wall Street Journal reports that United said the AI tools risk exposing sensitive customer information and could trigger purchases customers didn’t intend to make. The airline also pointed to a legal problem: Federal Aviation Administration and Transportation Department rules require airlines to present certain information to customers directly, something an automated agent can’t always do. United gave one example: an AI agent cannot attest during check-in that a passenger’s bags don’t contain explosives. Under the new policy, AI agents including Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots will still be able to pull up United’s flight options and prices for a customer. What they won’t be able to do is finish the transaction on United’s website. United said its back-end technology can already tell whether a booking came from an individual, a traditional travel agency, or an AI agent, and that for now, it isn’t seeing many bookings coming through AI agents at all. The airline said it will keep evaluating the tools as personal AI assistants evolve. United joins Amazon in keeping purchasing bots at arm’s length, a more cautious stance than other major U.S. carriers have taken. None have publicly moved against AI agents. Southwest Airlines launched a ChatGPT plug-in earlier this year that lets customers search its flight inventory through the chatbot. Delta said AI assistants can complete bookings once authenticated, with extra safeguards applied to “sensitive transactions” such as trips booked for unaccompanied minors. American Airlines said some AI agents, including Muse, can already buy tickets through certain partners, and that customers can direct an AI agent to complete a booking directly on American’s website. United CEO Scott Kirby addressed the company’s approach Tuesday at an event in Chicago. “To be honest, I don’t want to create another middleman,” he said. Kirby said he came to appreciate AI’s potential after building his own sports betting app by vibe-coding it, a process that took three hourly sessions with a tutor. United also issued a broader call to other companies: “consider measures that preserve the data and security of their customers and strengthen safety.” The announcement comes as interest in AI-driven travel booking picks up elsewhere in the industry. OpenAI this week purchased Odessia, a startup building AI tools for booking travel. Last month, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said travel planning ranks among the top use cases for the company’s Muse agent. Companies are racing to build out AI booking capabilities, but actual usage so far looks thin. Uber Technologies said that during the busy Halloween week earlier this month, its drivers completed 320 million trips combined across Uber and Uber Eats. Unlike a standard AI chatbot that answers questions and waits for the next prompt, an AI agent can take actions in the world: logging into accounts, searching for products, filling out forms, completing purchases, sending messages, and managing files, often with little or no additional input after the initial instruction.Examples include Meta's Muse, OpenAI's ChatGPT Dots, and Anthropic's Claude-based agentic workflows, all of which have been built to handle multi-step tasks across connected apps and services.
The defining characteristic of an agent is that it acts rather than just responds, and it can do so across a session that spans many steps and potentially many different services.

For businesses receiving agent-driven traffic, the concerns center on security, liability, and the dilution of direct consumer relationships.How Do AI Agents Affect the Industry?The question of how AI agents interact with commerce and service businesses is unresolved and playing out in real time across multiple industries simultaneously.

Businesses like United, JPMorgan Chase, and Amazon have moved to block agents over concerns ranging from security and fraud to regulatory compliance and the loss of direct customer relationships.At the same time, other companies including Southwest Airlines are actively building integrations that invite agents into their booking flows.The adoption rate among consumers is still modest: Uber reported that during the week of Halloween 2026, its 320 million trips and deliveries included only 500 AI-agent-driven Uber Eats orders and four rides, suggesting that agentic commerce remains a niche use case despite significant industry attention.

The core tension for the industry is between the genuine convenience AI agents could offer consumers and the significant unresolved questions around data security, regulatory compliance, and who bears responsibility when an AI agent makes a mistake or causes harm during a transaction.

extraction.description: United Airlines is now beginning its move to block AI agents from booking flights on its website and via third party platforms.

Businesses like United, JPMorgan Chase, and Amazon have moved to block agents over concerns ranging from security and fraud to regulatory compliance and the loss of direct customer relationships.At the same time, other companies including Southwest Airlines are actively building integrations that invite agents into their booking flows.The adoption rate among consumers is still modest: Uber reported that during the week of Halloween 2026, its 320 million trips and deliveries included only 500 AI-agent-driven Uber Eats orders and four rides, suggesting that agentic commerce remains a niche use case despite significant industry attention.

"To be honest, I do not want to create another middleman," Kirby said, articulating a concern that AI agents sitting between United and its customers could erode the direct relationship the airline has built through its own app, website, and loyalty program.Transportation Department, FAA Also Against AI AgentsBeyond United's own business concerns, the airline specifically cited existing federal regulations from the Department of Transportation and the Federal Aviation Administration as reasons why AI agent bookings raise compliance problems that go beyond corporate preference, said Engadget.The FAA and DOT have regulations governing the interaction between airlines and passengers during the booking and check-in process, some of which explicitly require a human acknowledgment or disclosure.

For businesses receiving agent-driven traffic, the concerns center on security, liability, and the dilution of direct consumer relationships.How Do AI Agents Affect the Industry?The question of how AI agents interact with commerce and service businesses is unresolved and playing out in real time across multiple industries simultaneously.

The plugin is built to allow Southwest to appear earlier in the customer journey and offer a more direct path from intent to booking, with the airline viewing the AI-assisted channel as a way to reach customers where they are already searching.The difference in approach between United and Southwest illustrates that there is no industry-wide consensus on how to handle agentic commerce in travel.

extraction.body: Bitcoin fell below its 200-day average to about $71,180, its lowest since August, as about $475 million in long bets were liquidated and Nvidia's CEO resigned. Bitcoin broke its 200-day moving average near $73,136 early Thursday and fell to about $71,180, its lowest since Aug. 20, CoinMarketCap data show. About $475 million in long positions were liquidated across crypto markets in four hours, CoinGlass data show, as Nvidia's CEO resigned and the 10-year Treasury yield topped 5%. Bitfinex says Bitcoin won back the cost basis of recent buyers within two weeks in 11 of 14 breaks below it since 2016, which puts the two-week checkpoint on Nov. 22. A CryptoQuant contributor set out the next test on Wednesday. Bitcoin traded at $71,346 at 10:28 a.m. ET on Thursday, CoinMarketCap data show. It slipped below the 200-day average early in the morning, hours before the US open. The 200-day average smooths out daily swings, and traders watch it as a dividing line for the longer-term trend. Bitcoin last closed below it in August. Futures selling is doing most of the damage. CryptoQuant contributor RugaResearch estimates that Bitcoin demand has turned sharply negative, with spot buying improving while perpetual futures drag. Bitcoin fell further than the Nasdaq, where Nvidia's own shares recovered part of their early loss. Spot holders are selling at a loss, but more slowly than earlier in the year, Bitfinex analysts wrote. Leveraged traders have kept buying the dip instead. After Tuesday's inflation data, about $729 million of liquidations barely dented open interest, they wrote. Large holders have also stepped in. Glassnode found some large wallets buying last week. Bitcoin has lost the cost basis of recent buyers, near $75,700 by Bitfinex's measure, 14 times since 2016 after long stretches above it. It won that level back within two weeks in 11 of those cases. Glassnode's map puts the largest cluster of leveraged positions near $60,000.

extraction.body: Bitcoin costs around $73,630 on Tuesday evening, roughly €65,960. On the Kraken exchange the price fell as low as $72,585 during the day, its lowest level since August 20. Whether the range between $72,000 and $75,000 holds depends on three things: the 200-day moving average at around $73,150, the outflows from the US funds and whether the US Federal Reserve raises rates in December. What is established: US consumer prices rose more than expected in October, long positions worth around $178 million were forcibly closed within an hour, and the spot ETFs lost money on four of the five trading days of the previous week. Our assessment follows further down: the zone holds only if the fund outflows dry up, and so far there is no sign of that. Where the price could head over the coming months is covered in our bitcoin price prediction. Bitcoin back at its August 20 level: the autumn rally has been wiped out To understand why the area around $73,000 in particular is getting so much attention, you have to go back almost three months. On August 19, bitcoin's low on Kraken was still $64,116. Two days later the daily close was $73,001, a jump of almost 14 percent in 48 hours. Since August 21 the price had not dropped below that mark on a single day, until this Tuesday. Arithmetically, the entire late-summer rise has thus been given back. The 30-day high was $84,840, and the price is now a good 13 percent below it. It is around 42 percent short of the record high of $126,080 from October 6, 2025. Over seven days the price is down 5.3 percent, over 30 days 12.2 percent, both according to CoinGecko data. On Monday bitcoin had still closed at $75,253. In our bitcoin price prediction of November 9, the price stood just below the average of $75,451 at which Strategy bought its holdings. New additions are the inflation report and a daily low that, for the first time since late summer, was below the 200-day moving average. US inflation in October: 0.4 percent instead of 0.3 percent The trigger for Tuesday afternoon's decline was the US consumer price index. Prices rose 0.4 percent month on month in October against an expected 0.3 percent. The core rate excluding energy and food rose 0.3 percent, against a forecast of 0.2 percent. The core rate has thus been running at this pace since August, as CoinMarketCap sums up. Fed governor Christopher Waller had said beforehand that with a core rate like this, a 50 basis point hike in December should also be considered. For bitcoin that is an unfavourable backdrop: higher rates make safe assets such as US Treasuries more attractive and raise the cost of the credit used for leverage on the futures markets. US inflation ran hotter than expected in October, and with it the bets on a rate hike in December. Liquidations: $178 million in long positions in one hour How fragile the market was became clear in the hour after the release. According to CoinGlass data, bets on rising prices worth around $178 million were forcibly closed during that time. A liquidation happens when the collateral posted for a leveraged trade is no longer sufficient: the exchange then sells the position itself, and that sale pushes the price down further. The funding rate on perpetual futures at Deribit has been only just above zero for a week, most recently at around 0.004 percent per eight hours. The futures market is no longer overheated, and part of the leverage has already been squeezed out of the market. Analytics firm Glassnode describes the situation in similar terms: selling from the ETFs and nervous short-term holders are weighing on the price, but part of the leverage has already been flushed out. ETF outflows: $1.28 billion in one week The main reason recoveries are fizzling out quickly at the moment lies with the US spot ETFs. In the previous week the funds lost a net $1.282 billion according to SoSoValue data, the largest weekly outflow since the end of June. Monday added a further $201 million in outflows, $213 million of it from BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust alone, while smaller funds took in a little. Since the start of the year the funds thus show a balance of minus $914 million. As recently as September 22 the annual tally had turned positive, after more than $6 billion of inflows since the start of August, CoinDesk reports. In each of the two previous years the funds had collected more than $20 billion.

extraction.body: Bitcoin (BTC) dropped below $73,000 in morning trade on Thursday for the first time since August as the turmoil around Nvidia (NVDA) dragged on tech stocks, taking cryptocurrencies and crypto-linked equities with it. Bitcoin’s price fell 1.5% in the last 24 hours, falling to around $72,900 at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the apex cryptocurrency trended in ‘extremely bearish’ territory over the past day. Crypto analyst Michael van de Poppe said in a post on X that Bitcoin has support at its 200-day moving average and another support zone between $70,000 and $71,500. However, he stated that buyers might not be strong enough to push the price through resistance yet. “What I'd like to see: A sweep of the lows towards the lower support zones and then a high-volume candle + reclaim back upwards,” he said, calling it “a strong trigger for trades.” The overall cryptocurrency market slipped around 2% in the last 24 hours, teetering above the $2.5 trillion mark with NVDA stock down over 7% and the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) falling almost 2.5%. Analysts were mulling over whether CEO Jensen Huang would be able to retain his post and, if he were removed, who would take the helm instead, after reports stated that he had a second affair with an executive within the company. Ethereum (ETH), Solana (SOL), and Ripple’s XRP (XRP) also fell alongside Bitcoin. Ethereum’s price fell 1.8% in the last 24 hours, struggling to hold above the $2,000 mark, while Solana’s price also fell 1.8%, in danger of dropping below $80. XRP’s price was down around 2%, trading just above the $1 mark. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Ethereum improved to ‘bearish’ from ‘extremely bearish’ territory over the past day, while sentiment around XRP and Solana remained in the ‘bearish’ zone. Crypto equities fell alongside cryptocurrencies in pre-market on Thursday. Corporate cryptocurrency treasuries Strategy (MSTR), Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR), and Strive (ASST) took the biggest hits. MSTR stock was down nearly 6%, while BMNR stock and ASST shares both dropped around 5.5% each. Strategy faces an additional source of pressure after MSCI said it would remove the company from its global indexes after the November 30 rebalancing. The decision could prompt passive funds tracking those indexes to sell their holdings. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around MSTR trended in ‘bearish’ territory over the past day, while chatter rose to ‘normal’ from ‘low’ levels. Large-cap crypto equities Coinbase (COIN) and USDC stablecoin issuers (CRCL) were also caught in the selloff. COIN stock fell around 4%, while CRCL shares were down around 3.5% in pre-market trade. Bitcoin miners, many of which have turned to renting out power and space to AI data centers, were caught on both sides of the sell-off. Cipher Digital (CIFR) fell 5.1%, Mara Holdings (MARA) 4.6%, Hut 8 (HUT) 4.3%, TeraWulf (WULF) 4%, and CleanSpark (CLSK) 3.9%. Select market data provided by ICE Data Services . extraction.body: Bitcoin fell below its 200-day average to about $71,180, its lowest since August, as about $475 million in long bets were liquidated and Nvidia's CEO resigned. Bitcoin broke its 200-day moving average near $73,136 early Thursday and fell to about $71,180, its lowest since Aug. 20, CoinMarketCap data show. About $475 million in long positions were liquidated across crypto markets in four hours, CoinGlass data show, as Nvidia's CEO resigned and the 10-year Treasury yield topped 5%. Bitfinex says Bitcoin won back the cost basis of recent buyers within two weeks in 11 of 14 breaks below it since 2016, which puts the two-week checkpoint on Nov. 22. A CryptoQuant contributor set out the next test on Wednesday. Bitcoin traded at $71,346 at 10:28 a.m. ET on Thursday, CoinMarketCap data show. It slipped below the 200-day average early in the morning, hours before the US open. The 200-day average smooths out daily swings, and traders watch it as a dividing line for the longer-term trend. Bitcoin last closed below it in August. Futures selling is doing most of the damage. CryptoQuant contributor RugaResearch estimates that Bitcoin demand has turned sharply negative, with spot buying improving while perpetual futures drag. Bitcoin fell further than the Nasdaq, where Nvidia's own shares recovered part of their early loss. Spot holders are selling at a loss, but more slowly than earlier in the year, Bitfinex analysts wrote. Leveraged traders have kept buying the dip instead. After Tuesday's inflation data, about $729 million of liquidations barely dented open interest, they wrote. Large holders have also stepped in. Glassnode found some large wallets buying last week. Bitcoin has lost the cost basis of recent buyers, near $75,700 by Bitfinex's measure, 14 times since 2016 after long stretches above it. It won that level back within two weeks in 11 of those cases. Glassnode's map puts the largest cluster of leveraged positions near $60,000.

Bitcoin traded at $71,346 at 10:28 a.m. ET on Thursday, CoinMarketCap data show. It slipped below the 200-day average early in the morning, hours before the US open.

Futures selling is doing most of the damage. CryptoQuant contributor RugaResearch estimates that Bitcoin demand has turned sharply negative, with spot buying improving while perpetual futures drag.
Bitcoin fell further than the Nasdaq, where Nvidia's own shares recovered part of their early loss.
Spot holders are selling at a loss, but more slowly than earlier in the year, Bitfinex analysts wrote. Leveraged traders have kept buying the dip instead.
After Tuesday's inflation data, about $729 million of liquidations barely dented open interest, they wrote.
Large holders have also stepped in. Glassnode found some large wallets buying last week.
Bitcoin has lost the cost basis of recent buyers, near $75,700 by Bitfinex's measure, 14 times since 2016 after long stretches above it. It won that level back within two weeks in 11 of those cases.
Glassnode's map puts the largest cluster of leveraged positions near $60,000.

extraction.body: Bitcoin costs around $73,630 on Tuesday evening, roughly €65,960. On the Kraken exchange the price fell as low as $72,585 during the day, its lowest level since August 20. Whether the range between $72,000 and $75,000 holds depends on three things: the 200-day moving average at around $73,150, the outflows from the US funds and whether the US Federal Reserve raises rates in December. What is established: US consumer prices rose more than expected in October, long positions worth around $178 million were forcibly closed within an hour, and the spot ETFs lost money on four of the five trading days of the previous week. Our assessment follows further down: the zone holds only if the fund outflows dry up, and so far there is no sign of that. Where the price could head over the coming months is covered in our bitcoin price prediction. Bitcoin back at its August 20 level: the autumn rally has been wiped out To understand why the area around $73,000 in particular is getting so much attention, you have to go back almost three months. On August 19, bitcoin's low on Kraken was still $64,116. Two days later the daily close was $73,001, a jump of almost 14 percent in 48 hours. Since August 21 the price had not dropped below that mark on a single day, until this Tuesday. Arithmetically, the entire late-summer rise has thus been given back. The 30-day high was $84,840, and the price is now a good 13 percent below it. It is around 42 percent short of the record high of $126,080 from October 6, 2025. Over seven days the price is down 5.3 percent, over 30 days 12.2 percent, both according to CoinGecko data. On Monday bitcoin had still closed at $75,253. In our bitcoin price prediction of November 9, the price stood just below the average of $75,451 at which Strategy bought its holdings. New additions are the inflation report and a daily low that, for the first time since late summer, was below the 200-day moving average. US inflation in October: 0.4 percent instead of 0.3 percent The trigger for Tuesday afternoon's decline was the US consumer price index. Prices rose 0.4 percent month on month in October against an expected 0.3 percent. The core rate excluding energy and food rose 0.3 percent, against a forecast of 0.2 percent. The core rate has thus been running at this pace since August, as CoinMarketCap sums up. Fed governor Christopher Waller had said beforehand that with a core rate like this, a 50 basis point hike in December should also be considered. For bitcoin that is an unfavourable backdrop: higher rates make safe assets such as US Treasuries more attractive and raise the cost of the credit used for leverage on the futures markets. US inflation ran hotter than expected in October, and with it the bets on a rate hike in December. Liquidations: $178 million in long positions in one hour How fragile the market was became clear in the hour after the release. According to CoinGlass data, bets on rising prices worth around $178 million were forcibly closed during that time. A liquidation happens when the collateral posted for a leveraged trade is no longer sufficient: the exchange then sells the position itself, and that sale pushes the price down further. The funding rate on perpetual futures at Deribit has been only just above zero for a week, most recently at around 0.004 percent per eight hours. The futures market is no longer overheated, and part of the leverage has already been squeezed out of the market. Analytics firm Glassnode describes the situation in similar terms: selling from the ETFs and nervous short-term holders are weighing on the price, but part of the leverage has already been flushed out. ETF outflows: $1.28 billion in one week The main reason recoveries are fizzling out quickly at the moment lies with the US spot ETFs. In the previous week the funds lost a net $1.282 billion according to SoSoValue data, the largest weekly outflow since the end of June. Monday added a further $201 million in outflows, $213 million of it from BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust alone, while smaller funds took in a little. Since the start of the year the funds thus show a balance of minus $914 million. As recently as September 22 the annual tally had turned positive, after more than $6 billion of inflows since the start of August, CoinDesk reports. In each of the two previous years the funds had collected more than $20 billion.

Bitcoin’s price fell 1.5% in the last 24 hours, falling to around $72,900 at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the apex cryptocurrency trended in ‘extremely bearish’ territory over the past day. Crypto analyst Michael van de Poppe said in a post on X that Bitcoin has support at its 200-day moving average and another support zone between $70,000 and $71,500. However, he stated that buyers might not be strong enough to push the price through resistance yet. “What I'd like to see: A sweep of the lows towards the lower support zones and then a high-volume candle + reclaim back upwards,” he said, calling it “a strong trigger for trades.” The overall cryptocurrency market slipped around 2% in the last 24 hours, teetering above the $2.5 trillion mark with NVDA stock down over 7% and the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) falling almost 2.5%. Analysts were mulling over whether CEO Jensen Huang would be able to retain his post and, if he were removed, who would take the helm instead, after reports stated that he had a second affair with an executive within the company. Ethereum (ETH), Solana (SOL), and Ripple’s XRP (XRP) also fell alongside Bitcoin. Ethereum’s price fell 1.8% in the last 24 hours, struggling to hold above the $2,000 mark, while Solana’s price also fell 1.8%, in danger of dropping below $80. XRP’s price was down around 2%, trading just above the $1 mark. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Ethereum improved to ‘bearish’ from ‘extremely bearish’ territory over the past day, while sentiment around XRP and Solana remained in the ‘bearish’ zone. Crypto equities fell alongside cryptocurrencies in pre-market on Thursday. Corporate cryptocurrency treasuries Strategy (MSTR), Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR), and Strive (ASST) took the biggest hits. MSTR stock was down nearly 6%, while BMNR stock and ASST shares both dropped around 5.5% each. Strategy faces an additional source of pressure after MSCI said it would remove the company from its global indexes after the November 30 rebalancing. The decision could prompt passive funds tracking those indexes to sell their holdings. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around MSTR trended in ‘bearish’ territory over the past day, while chatter rose to ‘normal’ from ‘low’ levels. Large-cap crypto equities Coinbase (COIN) and USDC stablecoin issuers (CRCL) were also caught in the selloff. COIN stock fell around 4%, while CRCL shares were down around 3.5% in pre-market trade. Bitcoin miners, many of which have turned to renting out power and space to AI data centers, were caught on both sides of the sell-off. Cipher Digital (CIFR) fell 5.1%, Mara Holdings (MARA) 4.6%, Hut 8 (HUT) 4.3%, TeraWulf (WULF) 4%, and CleanSpark (CLSK) 3.9%. Select market data provided by ICE Data Services . extraction.body: Firms tied to the Megaspeed controlling shareholder backed the Chinese AI lab as US scrutiny of her Nvidia chip network grows Thu 12 Nov 2026 · 10:06 EST · 3 min read Companies connected to Alice Huang have invested in DeepSeek , the Chinese AI lab known for its competitive open-source models. They also promised it access to Nvidia chips. The timing is awkward. Huang’s main vehicle, Singapore-based Megaspeed International, is already under US investigation over large-scale Nvidia chip imports estimated in the billions of dollars. Huang is a Chinese businesswoman who spent her earlier career in Shanghai’s finance and investment management sectors. She later moved into cloud infrastructure. In March 2023, she became the controlling shareholder of Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud-computing firm. She also served briefly as its managing director. Megaspeed moved quickly after the change in control. The company became an official Nvidia cloud partner shortly after Huang took over. In early 2025, Huang and her associates pitched data-center projects across Southeast Asia. The selling point was guaranteed access to Nvidia GPUs, the graphics processors that power most large-scale AI training and inference. Huang’s network has reportedly facilitated Nvidia AI chip transactions worth billions of dollars. Those deals reportedly involved models such as the H100 and H200, two of Nvidia’s flagship AI accelerators. The DeepSeek investments arrived around November 12, 2026. Firms associated with Huang put money into the lab, with a promise of Nvidia chips attached. Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy. We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime. The problem is everything surrounding the deal. US authorities are examining Megaspeed’s operations, and the investigation centers on the very chip imports that would make such a promise possible. Nvidia’s board has also been reviewing related matters. The chipmaker now finds one of its official cloud partners at the center of a story about chip flows and Chinese AI development. Discussions about possible intelligence ties to Huang’s operations have also surfaced alongside the investment news. Those questions remain open, and nothing in the available material establishes them as fact. Huang’s current status is unclear. Media attention on her business dealings has intensified as the pieces of this network come into view. A Singapore-registered company with an official Nvidia partnership, controlled by a Chinese businesswoman, moving billions of dollars in high-end GPUs, is precisely the type of arrangement regulators tend to examine closely. Add a stake in a leading Chinese AI lab, and the picture becomes harder to explain away as routine cloud business. That does not mean wrongdoing has been proven. The investigations are ongoing, and the intelligence-related questions are still just questions. For Nvidia, the stakes are reputational and potentially regulatory. Its partner program is supposed to signal trust, and a partner under investigation for multibillion-dollar chip imports tests that signal. The board’s review suggests the company is taking the matter seriously. How that review concludes, and whether Megaspeed keeps its partner status, will be worth watching. The key items to track are the outcome of the US investigations into Megaspeed, the result of Nvidia’s board review and any clarification of Huang’s whereabouts and role.
