Built on the company's Blackwell GPU microarchitecture, it succeeds the older Hopper architecture and is designed to power large-scale artificial intelligence, heavy-duty data centres and high-performance computing.Alice, also known as Alice Wang or Huang Le, is a Chinese businesswoman whose links with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed have come under scrutiny.Meanwhile, Singapore authorities have issued Alice a stern warning and barred her from re-entering the country after finding that she provided inaccurate information during investigations into Megaspeed.Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said the Singapore Police Force (SPF) assessed that Alice had attempted to mislead investigators to downplay her role in the company.The probe centres on suspected false declarations involving the purchase of servers and other related offences.

According to reports, she was introduced to Jensen through her husband, corporate investor Kang Weigh, around a decade before reports of her alleged relationship with the billionaire executive emerged.Kang had business dealings with Jensen in the 2010s while acquiring Chinese video game companies, a source familiar with the couple told The Information.Chinese media reports suggest that Kang and Alice used their association with Jensen to secure business opportunities over the years.

extraction.body: Firms tied to the Megaspeed controlling shareholder backed the Chinese AI lab as US scrutiny of her Nvidia chip network grows Thu 12 Nov 2026 · 10:06 EST · 3 min read Companies connected to Alice Huang have invested in DeepSeek , the Chinese AI lab known for its competitive open-source models. They also promised it access to Nvidia chips. The timing is awkward. Huang’s main vehicle, Singapore-based Megaspeed International, is already under US investigation over large-scale Nvidia chip imports estimated in the billions of dollars. Huang is a Chinese businesswoman who spent her earlier career in Shanghai’s finance and investment management sectors. She later moved into cloud infrastructure. In March 2023, she became the controlling shareholder of Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud-computing firm. She also served briefly as its managing director. Megaspeed moved quickly after the change in control. The company became an official Nvidia cloud partner shortly after Huang took over. In early 2025, Huang and her associates pitched data-center projects across Southeast Asia. The selling point was guaranteed access to Nvidia GPUs, the graphics processors that power most large-scale AI training and inference. Huang’s network has reportedly facilitated Nvidia AI chip transactions worth billions of dollars. Those deals reportedly involved models such as the H100 and H200, two of Nvidia’s flagship AI accelerators. The DeepSeek investments arrived around November 12, 2026. Firms associated with Huang put money into the lab, with a promise of Nvidia chips attached. Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy. We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime. The problem is everything surrounding the deal. US authorities are examining Megaspeed’s operations, and the investigation centers on the very chip imports that would make such a promise possible. Nvidia’s board has also been reviewing related matters. The chipmaker now finds one of its official cloud partners at the center of a story about chip flows and Chinese AI development. Discussions about possible intelligence ties to Huang’s operations have also surfaced alongside the investment news. Those questions remain open, and nothing in the available material establishes them as fact. Huang’s current status is unclear. Media attention on her business dealings has intensified as the pieces of this network come into view. A Singapore-registered company with an official Nvidia partnership, controlled by a Chinese businesswoman, moving billions of dollars in high-end GPUs, is precisely the type of arrangement regulators tend to examine closely. Add a stake in a leading Chinese AI lab, and the picture becomes harder to explain away as routine cloud business. That does not mean wrongdoing has been proven. The investigations are ongoing, and the intelligence-related questions are still just questions. For Nvidia, the stakes are reputational and potentially regulatory. Its partner program is supposed to signal trust, and a partner under investigation for multibillion-dollar chip imports tests that signal. The board’s review suggests the company is taking the matter seriously. How that review concludes, and whether Megaspeed keeps its partner status, will be worth watching. The key items to track are the outcome of the US investigations into Megaspeed, the result of Nvidia’s board review and any clarification of Huang’s whereabouts and role. sources.title: AWS Trainium Enhances AI Model Deployment with SGLang-Neuron Integration
passages: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has announced the public availability of SGLang-Neuron, a new integration designed to streamline the deployment of frontier artificial intelligence models on AWS Trainium chips.
SGLang-Neuron utilizes standard PyTorch operations for model execution.
By unifying the serving workflow with familiar SGLang interfaces and leveraging native PyTorch, the integration aims to accelerate AI development and deployment for a wide range of applications.

The SGLang core continues to manage the API server, request lifecycle, RadixAttention, and prefix-cache bookkeeping, while the plugin is responsible for Trainium-specific implementations of models, attention mechanisms, mixture of experts (MoE), and the graph runner.TorchNeuron integrates Trainium as a native PyTorch device.
Upon installation, the plugin registers the Neuron platform through SGLang's plugin entry points.
When starting the server, setting the environment variable SGLANG_PLATFORM=neuron directs SGLang to utilize this new platform.

This collaboration, involving RadixArk and Annapurna Labs, allows developers to leverage the familiar SGLang interface for serving models and generating reinforcement learning rollouts directly on AWS's specialized AI hardware.The Chenab Times has learned that SGLang-Neuron is accessible via an AWS Deep Learning Container, enabling users to maintain their existing SGLang workflows. This means that launching models and invoking endpoints using generation APIs remains unchanged, with SGLang-Neuron handling the underlying execution on AWS Trainium. The integration operates on native PyTorch, and its out-of-tree plugin architecture facilitates independent development and faster iteration between SGLang core and Trainium support.How SGLang Operates on AWS TrainiumSGLang-Neuron functions as an out-of-tree plugin that bridges SGLang with the AWS Trainium platform. Upon installation, the plugin registers the Neuron platform through SGLang's plugin entry points. When starting the server, setting the environment variable SGLANG_PLATFORM=neuron directs SGLang to utilize this new platform. The SGLang core continues to manage the API server, request lifecycle, RadixAttention, and prefix-cache bookkeeping, while the plugin is responsible for Trainium-specific implementations of models, attention mechanisms, mixture of experts (MoE), and the graph runner.TorchNeuron integrates Trainium as a native PyTorch device. SGLang-Neuron utilizes standard PyTorch operations for model execution. For enhanced performance, it incorporates kernels developed with the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI). These operations and kernels are compiled into executable programs using torch.compile, subsequently prepared and run by the graph runner during model serving.The system also supports Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) disaggregation. In this setup, a prefill server computes the prompt KV cache and transfers it to a decode server via NIXL over Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA). Both servers continue to use SGLang’s scheduling and request lifecycle management, while the plugin oversees the Trainium execution and the KV-cache transfer process.Deploying Models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-NeuronUsers can begin deploying models by utilizing a Trainium3 Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance and the pytorch-inference-sglang-neuronx container. The process involves starting the container, launching the SGLang model server with specific configurations for model path, tensor parallelism, expert parallelism, KV cache data type, context length, and memory fraction, and finally sending requests to the model server via its API endpoint.For instance, to serve the OpenAI gpt-oss-120b model, users would execute commands within the container to start the SGLang server, specifying parameters such as --model-path openai/gpt-oss-120b, --tp-size 8, and --ep-size 8, among others. Once the server is running, requests can be made to the /v1/chat/completions endpoint using standard cURL commands.Further details on setup, supported models, features, and configurations can be found in the SGLang-Neuron getting started guide and repository documentation.ConclusionThe introduction of SGLang-Neuron represents a significant step in making advanced AI model deployment more accessible and efficient on AWS Trainium. By unifying the serving workflow with familiar SGLang interfaces and leveraging native PyTorch, the integration aims to accelerate AI development and deployment for a wide range of applications.

Once the server is running, requests can be made to the /v1/chat/completions endpoint using standard cURL commands.Further details on setup, supported models, features, and configurations can be found in the SGLang-Neuron getting started guide and repository documentation.ConclusionThe introduction of SGLang-Neuron represents a significant step in making advanced AI model deployment more accessible and efficient on AWS Trainium. story.title: Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron - Amazon Web Services (AWS)

facts.text: Today, Amazon announced that SGLang-Neuron is publicly available and can be accessed through an AWS Deep Learning Container, released by RadixArk in collaboration with Annapurna Labs.
With SGLang-Neuron, you can serve models and generate reinforcement learning (RL) rollouts with SGLang on AWS Trainium using the same SGLang interface you use today.
Trainium is a portfolio of AWS AI chips that delivers strong economics for AI training and inference at scale.
Underneath that interface, SGLang-Neuron runs on native PyTorch.
With its out-of-tree plugin design, Trainium support and SGLang core develop independently and iterate faster.
Try it with your workloads, contribute through the project repository, and share feedback to help shape future model and feature support.
Installing the plugin registers the neuron platform through SGLang’s plugin entry points, and setting SGLANG_PLATFORM=neuron selects it when the server starts.
SGLang core continues to provide the API server, request lifecycle, RadixAttention, and prefix-cache bookkeeping.
The plugin implements the Trainium-specific models, attention, mixture of experts (MoE), and the graph runner.
TorchNeuron registers Trainium as a native PyTorch device.
SGLang-Neuron uses standard PyTorch operations for the model execution path and incorporates kernels written with the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) for performance.
SGLang-Neuron also supports PD disaggregation .
In this configuration, a prefill server computes the prompt KV cache and transfers it to a decode server using NIXL over Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) .
The decode server then generates the remaining tokens.

For additional information, please see the SGLang-Neuron getting started guide for setup instructions, and explore the repository documentation for supported models, features, and validated configurations.
